recipes.title: Spicy Snakehead Fish and Lotus Stem Soup
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 3 lemongrass stalks, cut into 2.5 cm pieces
800 g snakehead fish or catfish, cleaned, descaled, and cut into 2.5 cm pieces
200 g peeled and sliced lotus stem
4-6 dried red chiles, seeded and chopped
2 sawtooth cilantro (coriander) sprigs, chopped, to garnish

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring the water to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, shallots, tamarind, and salt and return to a boil.
Add the fish and lotus stem and cook for about 8 minutes, then remove from the heat.
Add the fish sauce, lemon juice, and chiles. Ladle into soup bowls, garnish with sawtooth cilantro, and serve.

recipes.title: Spicy Vegetable Soup
recipes.subtitle: North

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 100 g chayote shoots or young spinach

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in warm water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.
Pound the chiles, garlic, shallots, and salt in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and mix to combine.
Bring the broth to a boil in a large pan over medium heat, add the chili paste, and stir until dissolved. Add the dried fish and return to a boil.

Reduce the heat and simmer for 5-7 minutes, until the fish softens. Add the chayote shoots or spinach and the tomatoes and simmer, stirring occasionally, for another 3-4 minutes. Ladle into bowls and serve.

recipes.title: Salmon Sour Soup
recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 2 x 40 g salmon fillets, cut into 1 cm-thick slices
1 x 5 cm piece fresh ginger, peeled and julienned
1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
2 scallions (spring onions), cut into 2 cm lengths
4 dried red chiles, seeded, to garnish

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the paste, pound the black peppercorns, shallots, and cilantro roots in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and mix until thoroughly combined.
Bring the broth to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the paste and crushed shallots and boil for 1-2 minutes.
Add the salmon and ginger, return to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 2-3 minutes.
Add the tamarind, sugar, and fish sauce, followed by the scallions. Ladle into a soup bowl, garnish with the dried chiles, and serve.

Ladle into a soup bowl, garnish with the dried chiles, and serve.

recipes.title: Very Spicy Papaya and Young Coconut Soup

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 2 liters water Juice of 2 limes, strained
600 g mixed fruit, such as young papaya, young coconut meat, ripe banana, pineapple, and pickled bamboo
1 kg sea bass, mullet, or king mackerel fillets, cut into 2.5-5 cm pieces
1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar

lines: 1 garlic bulb, cloves separated and chopped

Bring the water to a boil in a large pan. Add the chili paste and lime juice and return to a boil, then add all the fruit.
Return to a boil, add the fish, and cook for 5 minutes. Season with the salt and sugar, ladle into soup bowls, and serve.

recipes.title: Spicy Vegetable and Fish Soup
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 500 g whole snakehead fish, cleaned, skinned, head and bones removed, and cut into 5 cm pieces
100 g pumpkin, cut into 2.5 cm slices
200 g angled gourd, peeled, halved, and cut into 2 cm-thick slices
10-15 young Ceylon spinach or ordinary spinach leaves

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the chili paste, pound the chiles, salt, peppercorns, fingerroot, shallots, and shrimp paste together thoroughly in a mortar with a pestle. Add the fish and pound again until smooth. Set aside.

Reduce the heat to medium, add the pumpkin and baby corn, and return to a boil for 5 minutes. Add the mushrooms, angled gourd, Ceylon spinach, ivy gourd leaves, if using, and basil. Serve.

recipes.title: Spicy-and-Sour Tilapia Soup
recipes.subtitle: Northeast

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 2 lemongrass stalks, coarsely crushed and cut into 5 cm lengths
600 g tilapia, cleaned, filleted, and cut into bite-size pieces
10-15 red and green bird's-eye chiles, pounded

Add the tilapia and cook for 3-4 minutes without stirring, until cooked.
Stir in the chiles and cilantro, ladle into bowls, and serve.

300 g eel, cleaned and cut into 5 cm lengths

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring the broth and 475 ml water to a boil in a large pan.
Add the fingerroot, kaffir lime leaves, galangal, lemongrass, garlic, shallots, and chile powder and return to a boil.
Add the eel and return to a boil. Add the fish sauce and tamarind puree and boil for 7-10 minutes, until the eel is tender.
Stir in the basil, if using. Ladle into bowls and serve.

recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 200 g uncooked shrimp (prawns), peeled and deveined, tails intact

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in warm water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.
Pound the chiles, fingerroot, peppercorns, and shallots in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and dried shrimp and mix until combined.
Bring 475 ml water and the chili paste to a simmer in a pan over low heat. Add the fish sauce, salt, and sugar and stir well.
Add the shrimp, pumpkin, angled loofah, watermelons, waxy corn, bottle gourd, and dried shrimp. Stir well and cook for 7-10 minutes. Add the lemon basil leaves and serve.

recipes.title: Dried Squid, Pork Rib, and Radish Soup
recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 2 × 30 g dried squid, sliced crosswise into 2 cm-wide pieces
400 g soft-bone pork ribs, cleaned and chopped into 4 cm pieces
400 g daikon (mooli) radish, peeled, halved lengthwise, and cut crosswise into 2 cm-thick pieces
3 scallions (spring onions), chopped into 4 cm lengths

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the dried squid in water for 10 minutes, then drain and set aside.
Bring 950 ml water, the salt, peppercorns, and cilantro roots to a boil over medium heat. Add the pork ribs and boil for 4-5 minutes, then add the daikon and boil for another 4-5 minutes.
Add the soy sauce and soaked squid. Reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 25-30 minutes, until the pork is tender.
Ladle into soup bowls, sprinkle with the cilantro and scallions, and serve.

recipes.title: Stuffed Squid Soup
recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 200-250 g small squid, cleaned, with tentacles removed and reserved

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Pound the garlic and peppercorns to a smooth paste. Transfer to a large bowl, add the pork and 1 teaspoon soy sauce, and mix well. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for 10-15 minutes.
Stuff the pork mixture into the squid cavities, then lightly score each squid once or twice.
Pour the broth and 350 ml water into a large pan. Add the cilantro root and salt and bring to a boil over medium heat. Add the stuffed squid and tentacles and cook for 8-10 minutes, or until cooked.
Add the remaining soy sauce and Chinese celery and stir a few times. Remove from the heat, ladle into soup bowls, and serve.

recipes.title: Fish Noodle Soup
recipes.subtitle: Central

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the noodles in water for 10 minutes, then drain and blanch in boiling water for 1 minute, or prepare according to the package directions. Drain and set aside.
Blanch the fish balls in boiling water for 2 minutes. Remove with a slotted spoon and set aside.
For the soup, combine the broth, cilantro roots, garlic, peppercorns, salt, soy sauce, and sugar in a pan. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 10 minutes.
Divide the noodles and bean sprouts among serving bowls. Pour about 300 ml soup into each bowl and top with the fish balls, fish cake, scallions, cilantro, and Fried Garlic. Serve.

recipes.title: Spicy Buffalo Meat Soup

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 11⁄4 kg buffalo meat or beef brisket, diced

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in warm water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.
Pound the chiles, peppercorns, shallots, garlic, lemongrass, galangal, and coriander seeds in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and pound again until combined.
Pour the water into a large pan, add the chili paste, and stir until dissolved. Bring to a boil over medium heat, add the buffalo or beef, and return to a boil.

Ladle into soup bowls, sprinkle with the cilantro, scallions, and sawtooth cilantro, and serve.

recipes.title: Oxtail Soup
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 2 kg oxtail, cut into 2.5-5 cm pieces
7 cm piece fresh ginger, peeled and sliced

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Put the cardamom pods, bay leaves, cilantro roots, garlic, and peppercorns into a herb infuser and set aside.

Bring 3 liters water to a boil over high heat. Add the oxtail and boil for 20-30 minutes, skimming away any scum. Add the herb infuser and cinnamon, reduce the heat to low, and simmer for 2 hours, or until the oxtail is tender.
Remove the oxtail and set aside. Strain the soup through cheesecloth into a clean pan and bring it back to a boil over medium heat, adding more water if necessary.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the onion and ginger and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes, until softened. Transfer to the soup, add the tomatoes, and cook for another 30 minutes.
Ladle into serving bowls and season with the fish sauce and lime juice. Garnish with the chiles, fried shallots, celery, scallions, cilantro, and lime wedges and serve.

recipes.title: Clear Soup with Pork Balls and Noodles
recipes.subtitle: Central
recipes.prepTime: 10 minutes, plus soaking and marrating times

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the noodles in a bowl of water for 5 minutes, or according to package directions. Drain, cut into short lengths, and set aside.
Mix the pork, 1 tablespoon sugar, and the soy sauce in a large bowl. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for 10-15 minutes. Add the noodles, mix together, shape into small balls, and set aside.
Bring the chicken broth to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the fish sauce and remaining sugar, then add the pork balls.
Reduce the heat and simmer for 4-5 minutes, or until the pork balls float to the surface. Ladle into soup bowls, sprinkle with the cilantro leaves, and serve.

lines: 700 g pork shoulder, cut into 3 cm cubes
4 pieces rock sugar or 1⁄2 tablespoon granulated sugar

ingredientGroups.heading: To garnish
lines: 40 g chopped scallions (spring onions) and cilantro (coriander)

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: To make the broth (stock) put the cinnamon stick, star anise, garlic, peppercorns and Cilantro (coriander) roots into an herb infuser.

Soak the vermicelli in a bowl of water for 10 minutes, then drain and blanch in a pan of boiling water for 1 minute or prepare according to package directions, until cooked. Drain.

Divide the vermicelli, fried garlic oil, cooked pork, and bean sprouts among serving bowls. Pour 350 ml of the broth into each bowl and garnish with the radish, scallions (spring onions), and cilantro (coriander). Serve.

recipes.title: Red Sauce Noodle Soup

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 daikon (mooli) radish, cut diagonally into 1 cm-thick slices

ingredientGroups.heading: For the soup
lines: 100 g water spinach, cut into 2.5 cm pieces
8 pieces cooked squid, cut into 2.5 cm pieces

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring the pork stock to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the cilantro roots, daikon, and salt and return to a boil. Boil for 5 minutes, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for another 5 minutes.
For the red sauce, put all its ingredients in a food processor with 75 ml water and process until smooth. Set aside.
For the pickled chiles, process all their ingredients in a food processor until smooth. Set aside.
Blanch the water spinach and rice noodles in boiling water for 1 minute, or prepare the noodles according to the package directions, then drain.

Divide the water spinach, noodles, squid, pig's blood curd, fish balls, tofu, red sauce, and pickled chiles among serving bowls. Pour 250 ml pork stock into each bowl, place a fried wonton on top, and serve.

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 2 Chinese fish cakes, cut into 2 cm pieces
2 tablespoons chopped salted dried cabbage leaves
4 tablespoons chopped salted radish fish sauce, to taste granulated sugar, to taste
50 g finely chopped scallions (spring onions) and cilantro (coriander), to garnish

ingredientGroups.heading: For the wontons
lines: 100 g wonton wrappers vegetable oil, for drizzling

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the roasted pork, combine the pork, Saam-Gler, oyster sauce, soy sauce, sugar, five-spice powder, and food coloring in a bowl. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator overnight, or for at least 2 hours.
Preheat the oven to 325°F/160°C. Put the pork in a roasting pan and roast for 45-55 minutes, or until cooked through. Let cool, then slice.

For the wontons, combine the pork, Saam-Gler, oyster sauce, soy sauce, and sugar in a bowl. Put 1 teaspoon of filling in the center of each wrapper, dampen the edges, and fold into a triangle. Cook the wontons in boiling water for 2-3 minutes, or until they float. Drain and drizzle with a little oil.
For the soup, bring the broth to a boil with the cilantro roots, garlic, peppercorns, salt, soy sauce, and daikon. Reduce the heat and simmer for 15-20 minutes.
Soak the rice noodles in water for 10 minutes, then blanch for about 1 minute, or cook according to the package directions. Drain. Blanch the ground pork for 2-3 minutes and drain.

Divide the noodles, roasted pork, wontons, blanched pork, Fried Garlic, fish cakes, peanuts, cabbage, and radish among six bowls. Add about 250 ml hot soup to each bowl. Season with fish sauce and sugar to taste, garnish with the scallion and cilantro mixture, and serve.

recipes.title: Pork Noodle Soup

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 200 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
140 g diagonally sliced yard-long beans, cut into 2 cm lengths

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the dried noodles in a bowl of water for 10 minutes, or according to package directions, until soft. Drain and set aside.

Bring a medium pan of water to a boil over medium heat. Add the pork loin, reduce the heat to a simmer, and cook for 8-10 minutes until cooked. Remove with a slotted spoon, drain in a colander, and let cool.
Return the pan of boiling water to the heat, add the pork liver, and cook for about 2 minutes until cooked. Drain, let cool, thinly slice, and cover.
Bring 75 ml water to a boil in a small pan over medium heat. Add the ground pork and stir for 1-2 minutes or until cooked. Drain and set aside, reserving the cooking water.
Heat the sugar and 120 ml water in another small pan over medium heat and stir until the sugar has dissolved and become syrupy. Set aside.
Blanch the yard-long beans in a pan of boiling water for 1 minute, then drain and set aside.

For the soup, put the cilantro roots, garlic, and black peppercorns in a cheesecloth herb bag. Pour the broth into a large pan, add the bag, and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer for 2-3 minutes.
For the sauce, mix the fish sauce, lime juice, peanuts, chili flakes, 11⁄2 tablespoons sugar syrup, 11⁄2 tablespoons ground pork, and the reserved cooking water in a bowl.
Cook the noodles in boiling water for 1 minute, or according to package directions, until soft. Drain and divide among serving bowls. Drizzle over the fried garlic oil and stir to combine.
Pour a little sauce and 350 ml soup into each bowl. Add the pork liver, sliced pork, eggs, yard-long beans, lettuce, scallion, and cilantro, then serve.

recipes.searchText: Pork Noodle Soup Central 300 g dried rice noodles 200 g pork loin 100 g pork liver, thinly sliced 100 g ground pork 200 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar 140 g diagonally sliced yard-long beans, cut into 2 cm lengths 2 cilantro roots, crushed 2 cloves garlic, coarsely crushed 11⁄2 teaspoons black peppercorns 1.7 liters chicken or pork broth 75 ml fish sauce 75 ml lime juice 50 g roasted peanuts, finely pounded 2 tablespoons chili flakes 3 tablespoons Fried Garlic Oil (see p. 64) 3 hard-boiled eggs, halved 2 lettuce leaves, coarsely chopped 25 g cilantro, finely chopped 1 scallion, finely sliced 11⁄2 teaspoons ground black pepper Soak the dried noodles in a bowl of water for 10 minutes, or according to package directions, until soft. Drain and set aside. Bring a medium pan of water to a boil over medium heat. Add the pork loin, reduce the heat to a simmer, and cook for 8-10 minutes until cooked. Remove with a slotted spoon, drain in a colander, and let cool. Return the pan of boiling water to the heat, add the pork liver, and cook for about 2 minutes until cooked. Drain, let cool, thinly slice, and cover. Bring 75 ml water to a boil in a small pan over medium heat. Add the ground pork and stir for 1-2 minutes or until cooked. Drain and set aside, reserving the cooking water. Heat the sugar and 120 ml water in another small pan over medium heat and stir until the sugar has dissolved and become syrupy. Set aside. Blanch the yard-long beans in a pan of boiling water for 1 minute, then drain and set aside. For the soup, put the cilantro roots, garlic, and black peppercorns in a cheesecloth herb bag. Pour the broth into a large pan, add the bag, and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer for 2-3 minutes. For the sauce, mix the fish sauce, lime juice, peanuts, chili flakes, 11⁄2 tablespoons sugar syrup, 11⁄2 tablespoons ground pork, and the reserved cooking water in a bowl. Cook the noodles in boiling water for 1 minute, or according to package directions, until soft. Drain and divide among serving bowls. Drizzle over the fried garlic oil and stir to combine. Pour a little sauce and 350 ml soup into each bowl. Add the pork liver, sliced pork, eggs, yard-long beans, lettuce, scallion, and cilantro, then serve.

recipes.title: Spicy Pork Soup with Straw Mushrooms
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 800 g pork short ribs, cut into bite-size pieces
15 red and green bird's eye chiles pounded

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring 1.2 liters water and the pork ribs to a boil in a large pan over medium heat, then reduce the heat and simmer for 40 minutes. Remove any scum with a slotted spoon. Drain and set aside.

Heat the broth (stock) in a pan over medium heat. Add the lemongrass, mushrooms, boiled meat, chiles, fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, and cilantro (coriander). Ladle into soup bowls, sprinkle with the fried shallots and chili flakes, and serve.

recipes.title: Spicy Pork and Madan Leaf Soup
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 kg boneless pork leg, cut into bite-size pieces
120 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
1.5 cm piece galangal, peeled and chopped
1 garlic bulb, cloves separated and chopped

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the chile paste, dry-fry the galangal, shallots, garlic, lemongrass, and cilantro root in a wok over medium heat for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Transfer to a mortar and pound with the dried chiles, salt, and shrimp paste.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the chile paste and sauté for 1 minute.
Add the pork, fish sauce, and sugar and mix well. Transfer to a pan, add the coconut milk, and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer for about 10 minutes, until the pork softens. Add the madan leaves and return to a boil. Ladle into bowls and serve.

recipes.title: Roasted Duck Noodle Soup
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: For the roasted duck
lines: 1 kg whole duck, cleaned and without giblets
11⁄4 tablespoons black salted soybeans, finely pounded

ingredientGroups.heading: For the soup
lines: 1 small cinnamon stick, broken into small pieces

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Preheat the oven to 300°F/150°C/Gas Mark 2.
Rinse the duck in cold water and pat dry. Rub it all over with the salt flakes and leave for 30 minutes. Rinse off the salt, pat dry, and set aside.

Pound the ginger, garlic, and cilantro roots until smooth. Mix with the five-spice powder, salted soybeans, salt, liquor or brandy, and sugar. Put the mixture inside the duck and place the duck on a roasting tray.

For the honey sauce, mix the honey, thick soy sauce, and 75 ml water. Brush the duck all over 2-3 times, then roast for about 13⁄4 hours, or until cooked, brushing with more sauce every 30 minutes. Cover with foil and rest for at least 15 minutes. Remove the drumsticks, carve the meat, and slice it into strips.

For the soup, heat the broth over medium heat. Put the star anise, cinnamon, garlic, cilantro roots, and black pepper in a spice bag and add it to the broth. Boil for 5 minutes. Season with soy sauce, salt, sugar, and dark soy sauce. Reduce the heat and simmer for 2-3 minutes.

Divide the noodles, bean sprouts, scallions, fried garlic, and duck among bowls. Pour about 250 ml soup into each bowl. Season to taste with vinegar, soy sauce, sugar, and chili flakes, if using, and serve.

recipes.title: Chicken and Coconut Soup
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 300 g black-skinned chicken breast or boneless chicken thigh, cut into 3 × 4 cm pieces
2 whole young coconuts, opened at the top and drained, with tops reserved as lids
4 dried red bird's-eye chiles, seeded, to garnish

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring the chicken broth and salt to a boil over medium heat.
Pound the cilantro root, shallot, lemongrass, galangal, and kaffir lime leaves to a paste. Add it to the pan and boil for 1-2 minutes.
Add the chicken and boil for 3-4 minutes, or until cooked. Add the young coconut flesh, fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, and coconut milk and cook for another 2 minutes.
Add the chopped chiles and cilantro. Ladle the soup into the whole young coconuts, garnish with Chili Jam oil and the dried chiles, and serve.

recipes.title: Spicy Chicken and Taro Soup
recipes.subtitle: North

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 300 g chicken, either half a whole chicken or boneless chicken thighs, cut into bite-size pieces
200 g taro, peeled and cut into 3 cm dice
20 g chopped scallions (spring onions), to garnish

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in warm water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.
Pound the chiles, peppercorns, garlic, shallots, and lemongrass to a smooth paste. Add the shrimp paste and mix to combine.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the chili paste and cook for 1 minute, or until fragrant. Add the chicken and stir-fry for 3-4 minutes.
Pour in the broth and bring to a boil. Add the taro and salt, reduce the heat to medium-low, and simmer for 4-5 minutes, or until the taro is tender.
Remove from the heat, ladle into soup bowls, garnish with the scallions and cilantro, and serve.

recipes.title: Pickled Lime
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 winter melon, peeled, seeded, and cut into 7 x 3 cm pieces

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak: the shiitake mushrooms in a bowl of hot water for 15 minutes, then squeeze to drain, slice into bite-size pieces, and set aside. Bring the broth (stock) and 750 ml water to a boil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add the chicken, cilantro (coriander) root, and salt and return to a boil. Remove any scum with a slotted spoon. Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 15 minutes. Add the pickled lime juice, pickled limes. and shiitake mushrooms, then simmer again for 10 minutes. Add the winter melon and soy sauce and continue to simmer for another 20 minutes or until the chicken and winter melon are tender. Stir gently. Ladle into soup bowls, sprinkle with white pepper, and serve.

recipes.subtitle: Northeast

lines: 2 lemongrass stalks, cut into 4 cm diagonal slices
1 whole 400 g chicken, chopped with the bone into small pieces

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring the broth (stock) and salt to a boil over high heat in a large pan. Add the galangal lemongrass, and shallots and boil for 1 minute. Had the chicken and return to a boil. Remove any scum with a slotted spoon. Reduce the heat and simmer for 15-20 minutes until cooked and tender. Add the fish sauce, kaffir lime leaves young tamarind leaves, tomatoes, and chiles Ladle into soup bowls and serve.

recipes.title: Daylily and Shiitake Mushroom Soup
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 250 g pork short ribs, cut into bite-size pieces
2 tablespoons goji berries salt, to taste

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring 1.2 liters water to a boil over medium heat. Add the pork ribs, white pepper, garlic, and cilantro roots and return to a boil. Skim, reduce the heat, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until tender.
Meanwhile, soak the daylily in water for 15-20 minutes. Rinse it 4-5 times under cold running water and squeeze dry. Discard the coarse stems and tie each daylily into a knot.
Add the daylily, shiitake mushrooms, and goji berries to the pan and simmer for about 10 minutes, or until the daylily has softened. Season to taste, ladle into bowls, and serve.

recipes.title: Shiitake and Stinkhorn Mushroom Soup
recipes.subtitle: Central

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring 1 liter water to a boil over medium heat. Add the pork ribs and return to a boil. Skim, reduce the heat, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until tender.

Meanwhile, soak the shiitake and stinkhorn mushrooms separately in hot water for about 15 minutes. Squeeze the softened shiitakes dry and cut into bite-size pieces. Rinse the stinkhorns to remove any dirt, squeeze dry, and cut into bite-size pieces.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the mushrooms and sauté for 1-2 minutes, or until dry. Season with some of the soy sauce, then remove from the heat.
When the pork-rib broth is clear, add the goji berries, red dates, salt, black pepper, and remaining soy sauce. When the ribs are tender, add the mushrooms. Ladle into bowls and serve.

recipes.title: Bitter Gourd and Pork Rib Soup
recipes.subtitle: Central

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Trim the ends from the bitter gourd. Halve it lengthwise and scrape out the seeds and white fiber, then halve each piece lengthwise again and cut crosswise into 5 cm lengths.
Dissolve 1 tablespoon salt in 475 ml water. Add the bitter gourd and soak for 15-30 minutes, then drain and rinse.

Pour 950 ml water into a large pan. Add the garlic, cilantro roots, peppercorns, and remaining 1 teaspoon salt and bring to a boil over high heat. Add the pork ribs and soy sauce and boil for 4-5 minutes.

Add the bitter gourd and boil for another 10 minutes without stirring, skimming any scum. Reduce the heat, cover, and cook for another 50-60 minutes, or until the pork is tender. Garnish with cilantro and serve.

recipes.title: Pork and Bottle Gourd Soup
recipes.subtitle: North

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 400 g pork tenderloin or short ribs, sliced

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring the water to a boil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add the pork, bottle gourd, sugar, and salt and cook for about 30 minutes.
Ladle into soup bowls, sprinkle with the scallions and cilantro, and serve.

recipes.title: Chinese Cabbage Soup
recipes.subtitle: North

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 300 g pork side (belly), cut into 2 cm-thick slices
250 g choy sum (Chinese flowering cabbage), cut into 6 cm strips

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Preheat the broiler (grill) to medium.
Pound the shallots, garlic, and shrimp paste in a mortar with a pestle to a fine paste.
Place the soybean sheet on a broiler pan and broil for about 2 minutes, until fragrant and dark brown. Let cool, then add it to the mortar and pound until ground.
Bring the water to a boil in a pan over medium heat. Add the pork and salt and boil for 20-30 minutes, until softened, skimming away any scum.
Add the paste, ground soybean sheet, tamarind, fish sauce, sugar, and cabbage and continue boiling for 4-5 minutes, until the cabbage is soft.
Ladle into soup bowls, sprinkle with the fried garlic and roasted chiles, and serve.

a handful of wild bitter gourd leaves or other bitter green leaves

steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in a bowl of warm water for 15 minutes or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.

2 handfuls of tree basil or holy basil leaves, chopped salt

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the chili paste, and cook for 1-2 minutes or until fragrant. Add the coconut milk and bring to a boil. Add the fish, cook for 4 minutes, then add the chiles, fish sauce, sugar, and a pinch of salt. Stir and cook for another 1-2 minutes or until the fish is fully flavored. Add the tree basil, stir a couple times, then serve.

recipes.title: Fried Sheatfish Curry
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 x 300 g small white sheatfish, cleaned, gutted
2 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
2-3 orange spur chiles, finely sliced diagonally

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Heat the oil for deep-frying in a wok or deep fryer to 350°F/180°C or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds. Deep-fry the fish for 8-10 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Set aside. Bring the coconut milk to boil in a clean wok over medium heat and add the chili paste. Stir for 2 minutes or until thoroughly combined and the coconut milk has thickened. Season with the fish sauce, sugar, and evaporated milk if using. Stir until the sugar has dissolved. Add the fish and cook for 1-2 minutes or until full-favored. Add the chiles and most of the basil leaves. Stir 3-4 times and remove from the heat. Garnish with the remaining basil leaves and serve.

1 × 1 kg sea bass, cleaned, filleted, and cut into 5 cm pieces
50 g red and green bird's-eye chiles, coarsely chopped

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring 1 liter water to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the shallots, garlic, salacca (snake fruit), and shrimp paste, return to a boil, then add the fish and cook for about 3 minutes. Remove from the heat, add the chiles and mint, and stir. Season with fish sauce and serve.

recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 × 300 g sea bass, cleaned, descaled, and cut into 2 cm-thick pieces
5 slices dried asam gelugor, washed, or 2-3 tablespoons lime juice
200 g heart of palm, cut into 5 cm strips, or cauliflower florets
20 dried red chiles, for the chili paste
1 teaspoon salt, for the chili paste
10 g garlic cloves, for the chili paste
1 × 5 cm piece long turmeric root, for the chili paste
11⁄2 teaspoons shrimp paste, for the chili paste

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in a bowl of warm water for 15 minutes or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.

Pound the chiles, salt, garlic, turmeric, and shrimp paste in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add about 2 tablespoons water and pound with a pestle until smooth. Set aside. Bring the broth (stock) to a boil in a pan over medium heat. Add the chili paste and boil for another 2 minutes. Add the sea bass, increase the heat to high, and return to a boil without stirring. Reduce the heat to medium and boil for another 2 minutes. Gently remove the fish from the pan and set aside.

Add the asam gelugor, fish sauce, and tamarind to the pan. Reduce the heat to low-medium and simmer for 5-7 minutes until the som khaek fully releases its sourness. Increase the heat back to medium, add the heart of palm or cauliflower, and boil for 2 minutes for the heart of palm or 3 minutes for the cauliflower until softened. Return the fish to the pan and boil for another 1 minute. Serve.

recipes.title: Jungle Fish Curry
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 90 g sliced yard-long beans or green beans, cut into 3 cm lengths
1 ×300 g sea bass or sea bream fillet, cut into 5 cm-thick slices
1 handful sweet basil leaves, plus extra to garnish

ingredientGroups.heading: For the chili paste
lines: 2.5 cm piece fresh galangal, peeled and finely chopped
1 teaspoon finely chopped kaffir lime zest

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the chili paste, soak the chiles in a bowl of warm water for 15 minutes or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.

Pound the chiles and salt in a mortar with a pestle until the chiles are fine flakes. Add the lemongrass and pound until smooth. Add the galangal and kaffir lime zest and pound thoroughly. Add the black peppercorns, garlic, and shallot and pound again, then add the cilantro (coriander) root and pound until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and pound until thoroughly combined and a smooth paste. Set aside. Bring 250 ml water and the chicken broth (stock) to a boil in a pan over high heat. Add 3 tablespoons of the chili paste, stir, and boil for 2-3 minutes. Add both eggplants (aubergines), the beans and baby corn, then reduce the heat to medium and boil for 3-4 minutes. Add the fish sauce, sugar, fingerroots, and finger chiles and stir a couple times. Gently add the fish and cook for 2-3 minutes, without stirring, until the fish is cooked. Add the basil and stir. Serve garnished with a few basil leaves.

recipes.title: Fish Curry in Banana Leaf
recipes.subtitle: Northeast

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 300 g Asian knifefish, bronze featherback, or sea bass fillet
50 g kaffir lime leaves, finely sliced
40 g sliced scallions (spring onions) banana leaves, for wrapping
To serve Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378) raw or steamed vegetables, such as cucumber, Chinese leaves, carrots, and yard-long beans

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Before cooking, check that the charcoal is glowing white-hot, or preheat a gas grill (barbecue) to 300°F/150°C.
Bring 475 ml water to a boil in a large pan over high heat. Add the fermented fish sauce, stir, then set aside and keep warm.

Pound half the sliced shallot in a mortar with a pestle. Add the fish and pound until smooth. Gradually pour in the warm fermented-fish water, stirring continuously. Gradually add the ground toasted rice and chili powder and mix well. Add the kaffir lime leaves, cilantro, scallions, and remaining shallot and stir until thoroughly combined.

Lay the banana leaves on a work surface. Put the fish curry in the center and flatten it slightly to make it easy to wrap. Cover with the sides of the leaf, fold over the ends, and secure with toothpicks.
Grill the banana-leaf package over low heat for 10-15 minutes, or until cooked. Unwrap and serve with rice and raw or steamed vegetables.

recipes.title: Dry Fish Curry
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 kg whisker sheatfish, red snapper, or red mullet, cleaned and tails removed
950 ml vegetable oil, for deep-frying, plus 60 ml
1 teaspoon ground white pepper Zest of 1⁄2 kaffir lime

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in warm water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.
Pound the chiles, shallot, garlic, galangal, fingerroot, and lemongrass in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and salt and pound again until thoroughly combined.

Cut each fish crosswise into 3 pieces. Heat the deep-frying oil in a wok or deep fryer to 340°F/170°C and fry the fish for about 7 minutes, until golden brown and crisp. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Heat the remaining 60 ml oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the chili paste and stir-fry for about 3 minutes, until fragrant.
Carefully add 120 ml water, then season with the fish sauce, sugar, and white pepper. Add the fried fish, stir, and cook for another 3-4 minutes. Garnish with the kaffir lime zest and serve.

200 g choy sum (Chinese flowering cabbage), chopped into 5 cm pieces

ingredientGroups.heading: To serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Put the fish in a steamer and steam for 5-7 minutes or until cooked. Remove from the steamer and remove and discard the skin. recipes.searchText: Fish Curry with Fermented Rice Noodles South 700 g snakehead fish, catfish, or sea bass fillet 3 tablespoon Southern Chili Paste (see p. 38) 1 liter coconut milk 21⁄2 tablespoons fish sauce 4 kaffir lime leaves, torn 1⁄2 teaspoon granulated sugar 1 kg cooked fermented rice noodles 100 g bean sprouts 300 g finely sliced yard long beans 1 lemongrass stalk, finely sliced 1 cucumber, sliced Put the fish in a steamer and steam for 5-7 minutes or until cooked. Remove from the steamer and remove and discard the skin. Pound the fish and chili paste in a mortar with a pestle until combined. Set aside. Bring the coconut milk to boil in a large pan over medium heat, add the chili paste mixture, and stir until thoroughly combined. Return to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for about 2 minutes. Season with the fish sauce, add the kaffir leaves, and simmer for another 5 minutes or until full-flavored. Remove from the heat and set aside. Divide the noodles among serving bowls and pour 175 ml of the curry into each bowl. Top with the bean sprouts yard-long beans, lemongrass, and cucumber and serve.

recipes.title: Spicy Fish Curry Bites
recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 tablespoon finely sliced kaffir lime leaves
1 red spur chile, cut into rings

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Put the fish meat, curry paste, fish sauce, and beaten egg in a large bowl and mix well, then while stirring, slowly pour in the coconut milk and stir until smooth.
Pour the mixture into a khanom krok pan or pancake puff pan, sprinkle with the kaffir lime leaves and chiles, then cover with the lids and put the pan over medium heat. Cook for 3-5 minutes. Serve.

recipes.title: Red Curry with Clams and Pineapple
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 500 g live Atlantic surf clams, cleaned, or 300 g clam meat
2 pineapples, peeled, cored, and cut into 2 cm pieces
2 tablespoons finely shredded kaffir lime leaves
1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
5 dried bird's-eye chiles, seeded, for the chili paste
4 dried red spur chiles, seeded, for the chili paste
1⁄2 teaspoon salt, for the chili paste
3 thin slices galangal, chopped, for the chili paste
2 lemongrass stalks, finely chopped, for the chili paste
2 small shallots, chopped, for the chili paste
2-3 garlic cloves, for the chili paste
1 teaspoon shrimp paste, for the chili paste

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in a bowl of warm water for 15 minutes or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.

Pound the chiles and salt in a mortar with a pestle until fine flakes. Gradually add the galangal, lemongrass, shallots, and garlic and pound until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and pound again until smooth and thoroughly combined. Set aside.

Put the clams in a wok or pan, cover with a lid, then steam over medium heat for 2 minutes or until the clam shells have opened and the clams begin to cook. Discard any clams that are still closed Let cool, then open the clams and remove the meat and set aside. Discard the shells.

Bring half the coconut milk to a boil in a pan over medium heat. Add 2 tablespoons of the chili paste, stir, and mix until the chili paste has dissolved and combined with the coconut milk. Boil for 3-4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until fragrant and the oil from the coconut milk has separated. Pour in the remaining coconut milk and return to a boil. Add the pineapple and cook for 5-7 minutes or until the pineapple has softened. Add the clam meat, fish sauce, kaffir lime leaves, and sugar, then gently stir and cook for another 2 minutes or until the sugar has dissolved. Serve.

recipes.title: Blue Crab and Coconut Milk Curry
recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 2 x 300 g live blue crabs, cleaned
11⁄2 teaspoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve Raw or steamed vegetables, such as sliced cucumber and round eggplants (aubergines), to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Put the crabs in the freezer for 20 minutes, then transfer them to a large bowl.

Working with one crab at a time, place it on a cutting board with its back down and legs facing upward. Raise the tail flap and push a small screwdriver or skewer through the hole underneath until it reaches the other side of the shell. Repeat with the second crab.
Remove the aprons and carapaces and rinse the crabs clean. Cut each crab in half vertically, then halve each piece horizontally. Remove and crush the claws.
Bring half the coconut milk to a boil in a pan over medium heat. Add the chili paste and stir continuously for 2-3 minutes, until fragrant.

Add the crab pieces, claws, and broth and boil for 2 minutes. Add the fish sauce, sugar, and remaining coconut milk, reduce the heat slightly, and boil gently for another 2-3 minutes, until the crab is cooked. Serve with rice and vegetables.

recipes.title: Stir-Fried Blue Crab Curry
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 2 x 300 g live blue crabs, cleaned
6 scallions, diagonally sliced into 4 cm lengths
100 g Chinese celery, cut into 4 cm lengths

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Put the crabs in the freezer for 20 minutes. Working with one crab at a time, place it on its back, raise the tail flap, and push a small screwdriver or skewer through the opening until it reaches the other side of the shell.
Remove the aprons and carapaces and rinse the crabs clean. Cut each crab in half vertically, then halve each piece horizontally. Remove and crush the claws.
Blanch the crab pieces and claws in boiling water for 2 minutes, until cooked, then drain.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the garlic and stir-fry for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the crab, increase the heat to medium-high, and stir-fry for 1 minute. Add the egg and stir-fry for about 10 seconds, until cooked.
Add the soy sauce, fish sauce, sugar, curry powder, broth or water, scallions, and celery. Stir-fry for another 1-2 minutes, until thoroughly mixed, and serve.

recipes.title: Shrimp and Vegetable Yellow Curry
recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 4 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
2 tablespoons Fried Shallots (see p. 84), to garnish Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring 350 ml coconut milk to a boil in a wok over medium heat. Add the curry paste, stir, and cook for 3-4 minutes or until fragrant and the texture has thickened. Add the fish sauce, sugar, tamarind, tomatoes, onion, 2 tablespoons water and the remaining coconut milk, and return to a boil. Reduce the heat slightly and cook for 2-3 minutes or until the tomatoes and onion have softened. Add the shrimp (prawns) and cook for another 3-4 minutes or until the shrimp are cooked. Add the snow peas (mangetout) and cook for 1 minute. Sprinkle with the fried shallots and serve with rice.

recipes.title: Spicy Coconut Milk Curry (Made from Field Crab)
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 75 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
4-5 kaffir lime leaves Salt, to taste
1 kg cooked rice noodles, to serve

ingredientGroups.heading: For the chili paste
lines: 1 garlic bulb, cloves separated and chopped

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in warm water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.
Pound the chiles, black pepper, garlic, shallots, turmeric, galangal, and lemongrass in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and pound again until smooth.
Pound the field crabs in the mortar to release their juices, then strain through a colander or sieve into a bowl and reserve the liquid.
Bring the coconut milk to a boil in a large pan. Add the chili paste and return to a boil.
Add the crab liquid, tamarind, sugar, and kaffir lime leaves, then season to taste with salt. Serve with the rice noodles.

recipes.title: Spicy-and-Sour Curry with Shrimp and Acacia Leaf Omelet
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 4 tablespoons Kaeng Som Chili Paste (see p. 36)
12 uncooked jumbo shrimp (king prawns), peeled and deveined, with tails still intact Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve

ingredientGroups.heading: For the deep-fried acacia leaf omelet

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the deep-fried acacia leaf omelet, rinse the acacia twigs and pick only the leaves and young stems.
Put the beaten eggs and acacia leaves and stems in a bowl and mix well with a fork.

Heat the oil for deep-frying in a large wok over medium heat. When fully heated, carefully pour in the acacia leaf mixture and cook for about 3 minutes on both sides or until golden brown and crispy. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Cut into 2.5 cm-square pieces and set aside.

Bring the broth (stock) to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the chili paste, and stir until the paste has dissolved. Return to a boil for 2-3 minutes, then season with the fish sauce, tamarind, sugar, and lime juice, if using. Return to a boil then add the acacia leaf omelet and shrimp (prawns). Cook for another 2-3 minutes or until the shrimp are cooked. Remove from the heat and ladle into serving bowls. Serve with rice.

recipes.title: Spicy-and-Sweet Curry
recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 200 g raw shrimp, peeled, deveined, and ground
11⁄2 teaspoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
8 green and red bird's-eye chiles Rice vermicelli, to serve
5 dried red spur chiles, for the chili paste
2 tablespoons vegetable oil, for the chili paste
5 garlic cloves, chopped, for the chili paste
5 shallots, chopped, for the chili paste
1⁄2 teaspoon salt, for the chili paste

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried spur chiles in warm water for 15 minutes, until rehydrated. Drain, chop, and set aside.
Toast the mung beans in a wok over medium heat for 5-6 minutes, until lightly browned and fragrant. Process them into fine flakes.

Heat the chili-paste oil in a wok over medium heat. Sauté the soaked chiles for 30 seconds, until fragrant and beginning to brown, then drain and set aside. Dry-fry the garlic and shallots for 5-6 minutes, until browned and fragrant.
Pound the sautéed chiles and salt in a mortar until smooth. Add the toasted garlic and shallots and pound again to a smooth paste.

Bring 475 ml coconut milk to a boil in a wok or pan over medium heat. Add the chili paste and sauté for 5-6 minutes, until the coconut oil separates. Add the ground shrimp and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes, until cooked.

Add the peanuts, mung beans, chicken broth, and remaining coconut milk. Season with the fish sauce, sugar, and tamarind. Reduce the heat and simmer for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the beans and peanuts are tender and fully flavored.
Meanwhile, heat the remaining oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Fry the whole bird's-eye chiles for 1-2 minutes, until darkened.
Serve the curry with rice vermicelli and top with the fried chiles.

recipes.title: Beef Massaman Curry
recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 500 g brisket or chuck beef, cut into 3 cm cubes
4 potatoes, peeled and cut into 4 cm pieces
1 small sweet potato, peeled and cut into 4 cm pieces
To serve Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378) or roti Cucumber Relish (see p. 35)

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring half the coconut milk and 100 ml water to a boil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add the beef and return to a boil, Reduce the heat, cover with a lid, and simmer for 50-60 minutes.

Meanwhile, heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the curry paste, and stir for 1-2 minutes or until sizzling and fragrant. Gradually add 150 ml coconut milk and stir for 2 minutes. Remove from the heat and set aside.

After the beef has finished simmering, add the paste, onions, peanuts, bay leaves, fish sauce, sugar, tamarind, cinnamon, cardamom pods, and the rest of the coconut milk and put over low-medium heat for 40 minutes. Add the potatoes and sweet potato, then reduce the heat to low, partly cover, and simmer for another 30-40 minutes or until the beef is tender. Serve with rice or roti.

recipes.subtitle: Central

lines: 200 g young watermelon or round zucchini, sliced into 2 cm-thick pieces
100 g yard-long beans, cut into 2.5 cm pieces
400 g raw shrimp, peeled and deveined with tails intact
4 dried red spur chiles, seeded, for the kaeng som paste
1⁄2 teaspoon salt, for the kaeng som paste
3 garlic cloves, for the kaeng som paste
3 shallots, chopped, for the kaeng som paste
1 teaspoon shrimp paste, for the kaeng som paste Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve

Season with the fish sauce, sugar, and tamarind. Add the shrimp and boil for 1-2 minutes, until just cooked.
Adjust with fish sauce, tamarind, and sugar so the curry tastes sweet, sour, and salty. Serve with jasmine rice.

recipes.subtitle: Central

lines: 400 g beef shank or rump, cut into bite-size pieces
1 teaspoon ground roasted cumin and coriander seeds Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve

ingredientGroups.heading: To garnish coconut cream
lines: 1 red spur chile, thinly sliced diagonally
a handful of sweet basil leaves

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the curry paste, soak the dried chiles in a bowl of warm water for 15 minutes or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.

Pound the chiles and salt in a mortar with the pestle until fine flakes form. Add the lemongrass, galangal, kaffir zest, shallots, garlic, cilantro (coriander) root, peppercorns, ground coriander, ground cumin, ground cardamom, and pound again until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and pound until combined Set aside.

Reduce the heat to low and simmer for another 4-5 minutes or until fully flavored. Add a swirl of coconut cream, garnish with the chile, kaffir lime leaves, and basil and serve with rice.

recipes.title: Beef and Coconut Milk Curry
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 5 red spur chiles, sliced diagonally lengthwise

ingredientGroups.heading: To serve
lines: 300 g water spinach, finely sliced and blanched

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the curry paste and sauté for 1-2 minutes, until fragrant.
Add 250 ml coconut milk and cook for 2-3 minutes, until the mixture thickens and the coconut oil separates and rises to the surface.
Add the beef and stir for about 4 minutes. Add 475 ml water and bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for about 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the remaining coconut milk, season with the fish sauce and sugar, and cook for another 5 minutes.
Add the eggplants and chiles, bring to a boil, and cook for 5 minutes. Add the basil, stir, and remove from the heat.
Serve with the rice vermicelli, bean sprouts, water spinach, and hard-boiled eggs.

recipes.searchText: Beef and Coconut Milk Curry Central 3 tablespoons vegetable oil 31⁄2 tablespoons Green Curry Paste (see p. 37) 600 ml coconut milk 500 g beef brisket, thinly sliced 21⁄2 tablespoons fish sauce 2 tablespoons granulated sugar 10-12 round eggplants (aubergines), quartered 5 red spur chiles, sliced diagonally lengthwise 2 handfuls sweet basil 500 g cooked rice vermicelli 250 g bean sprouts 300 g water spinach, finely sliced and blanched 3-4 hard-boiled eggs, halved Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the curry paste and sauté for 1-2 minutes, until fragrant. Add 250 ml coconut milk and cook for 2-3 minutes, until the mixture thickens and the coconut oil separates and rises to the surface. Add the beef and stir for about 4 minutes. Add 475 ml water and bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for about 20 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add the remaining coconut milk, season with the fish sauce and sugar, and cook for another 5 minutes. Add the eggplants and chiles, bring to a boil, and cook for 5 minutes. Add the basil, stir, and remove from the heat. Serve with the rice vermicelli, bean sprouts, water spinach, and hard-boiled eggs.

recipes.title: Spicy Beef and Vegetable Curry
recipes.subtitle: North

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 300 g chuck beef, thinly sliced into bite-size pieces

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the chile paste, pound the dried chiles, salt, shallots, garlic, lemongrass, galangal, long pepper, Sichuan peppercorns, coriander seeds, and dill seeds in a mortar until smooth.
Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the chile paste and sauté for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the beef, sliced galangal, lemongrass, and cilantro roots and stir-fry for 2 minutes, until the beef starts to cook.
Add the broth, fermented fish sauce, and fish sauce and simmer for 30 minutes, until the beef is tender.
Add the kaffir lime leaves, dill, skunk-vine tips, chile, and scallions and cook for another 1-2 minutes. Serve.

recipes.title: Beef Curry with Noodles
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 2 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
15 g peanuts, roasted and coarsely pounded
100 g extra-firm tofu, cut into small cubes

ingredientGroups.heading: For the yellow curry paste
lines: 4 cm piece fresh ginger, peeled and sliced

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the rice vermicelli in a bowl of water for 10 minutes or according to package directions then drain and set aside.

Meanwhile, for the curry paste, soak the dried chiles in a bowl of warm water for 15 minutes or until rehydrated, then drain and chop Dry-fry the garlic and ginger in a wok over medium heat for 5 minutes or until fragrant and brown. Set aside.

Pound the drained chiles and salt in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the lemongrass and galangal and continue to pound until thoroughly combined. Add the roasted garlic and ginger and pound until mixed well. Add the shallots and continue to pound, then add the spices and shrimp paste and pound to a smooth paste. Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat, add the curry paste, and saute for 2-3 minutes until fragrant. Remove from the heat and set aside. Bring 950 ml water and half the coconut milk to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the beef and return to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer for 40 minutes.
Add the remaining coconut milk and the broth (stock), and return to a boil. Add the fried chili paste, and season with the salt and sugar. Boil for about 5 minutes, then remove from the heat.

Cook the vermicelli in a pan of boiling water for 2 minutes or until soft. Drain and divide among serving bowls. Add 350 ml of the curried soup and 3-4 slices of beef to each serving bowl. Top with the salted turnips, bean sprouts, peanuts, tofu, fried shallots, and egg. Garnish with the cilantro (coriander) and scallions (spring onions) and serve.

recipes.title: Leftover Curry with Noodles
recipes.subtitle: North

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 90 g yard-long beans, cut into 3 cm lengths
150 g glass noodles, soaked and cut into 5 cm lengths

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the chile paste, soak the dried chiles in warm water for 15 minutes, then drain and chop.
Pound the chiles and salt in a mortar. Add the lemongrass, garlic, galangal, and shallot and pound until smooth.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the chile paste and sauté for 1 minute, until sizzling and fragrant.
Add the Hunglei curry and cook for 1 minute. Add the pea eggplants and yard-long beans and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the bamboo shoots and cook for 30 seconds. Add the noodles and fish sauce and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the ivy gourd leaves, kaffir lime leaves, cilantro, basil, and sugar and continue stirring for another minute, until thoroughly combined. Serve.

recipes.title: Spicy Pork Rib and Mushroom Curry
recipes.subtitle: North

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the curry paste, soak the dried chiles in a bowl of warm water for 15 minutes or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.

Pound the chiles, shallots, garlic, and shrimp paste in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Set aside. Bring the broth (stock) 475 ml water, and the salt to a boil in a large pan over high heat. Add the ribs and return to a boil. Remove any scum on the surface, Reduce the heat to low, cover the pan, and simmer for 30 minutes or until the ribs are tender.

Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat, add the curry paste, and sauté for 1 minute or until fragrant. Add the paste to the broth, then season with the fish sauce, oyster sauce, and sugar and cook for another 3-4 minutes. Add the acacia leaves, betel leaves, and mushrooms and simmer for 1 minute or until softened. Add the cilantro (coriander), stir, and serve.

recipes.title: Hunglei Curry
recipes.subtitle: North

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 200 g pork shoulder, cut into 2 cm pieces
250 g pork belly, cut into 2 cm pieces
15 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
4 cm piece fresh ginger, peeled and finely julienned
1 large clove garlic Steamed Jasmine Rice or Glutinous Rice (see p. 378), to serve
11⁄2 teaspoons Hunglei or ordinary curry powder

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the chile paste, soak the dried chiles in warm water for 15 minutes, then drain and chop.

Pound the chiles and salt in a mortar. Add the galangal and lemongrass and pound thoroughly. Add the garlic and shallots and pound to a paste, then add the shrimp paste and curry powder and pound until combined.
Mix both cuts of pork with the chile paste and pineapple. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour.
Heat the oil in a pan or casserole over medium heat. Add the marinated pork and sauté for 3-4 minutes, until fragrant.
Add 600 ml water, increase the heat, and boil for 10 minutes. Add the fish sauce, tamarind puree, sugar, peanuts, ginger, tomatoes, and garlic.
Partly cover, reduce the heat to medium-low, and simmer for 30-35 minutes, until the pork is tender and the liquid has reduced by half. Serve with rice.

recipes.title: Fermented Fish and Bamboo Shoot Curry
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 200 g canned bamboo shoots, cut into 2 cm dice
11⁄2 teaspoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Pound the lemongrass, galangal, shallots fingerroots, garlic, and shrimp paste together in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Set aside.

Bring the coconut milk to a boil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the paste and boil for 3-4 minutes or until fragrant. Add the pork side (belly), dried fish, and bamboo shoots, then boil for 5 minutes or until the pork is cooked through. Season with the fermented fish sauce, sugar, and salt and cook for another 2 minutes or until the bamboo shoots are fully flavored. Add the kaffir lime leaves and chopped chile and stir, then serve.

recipes.title: Pork and Cow Tree Leaf Curry
recipes.subtitle: Northeast

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 kg pork shoulder joint with fat, cut into bite-size pieces
225 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
500 g cow tree leaves or tamarind leaves

ingredientGroups.heading: For the chili paste
lines: 1 x 7 cm piece galangal, peeled and chopped
1 garlic bulb, cloves separated and chopped

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Mix the pork, sugar, salt, and soy sauce in a large bowl. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for 15 minutes.
For the chili paste, pound all its ingredients together in a mortar with a pestle until smooth.
Heat the oil in a large wok over medium heat. Add the chili paste and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes, until fragrant.
Add the pork and stir-fry for about 5 minutes, stirring continuously. Pour in the broth, bring to a boil, and boil for 10 minutes.
Reduce the heat to low, add the cow tree leaves, tamarind, and fish sauce, and simmer for 20-30 minutes, until the pork is tender. Serve.

recipes.title: Pork Curry with Siam Cardamom Shoots
recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 150 g thinly sliced Siam cardamom shoots or fresh ginger
300 g pork tenderloin or loin steak, thinly sliced
5 kaffir lime leaves, torn Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the cardamom shoots in a bowl of water for 1-2 minutes, then drain and set aside.

Bring half the coconut milk to a boil in a pan over medium heal. Add the chili paste and stir for 4-5 minutes or until fragrant and the coconut milk has thickened. Add the pork and cardamom shoots or ginger and cook for about 5 minutes or until the pork is cooked. Add the remaining coconut milk and season with the fish sauce, salt, sugar, and kaffir lime leaves. Return to a boil for 3-4 minutes, then serve with rice.

recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 11⁄2 teaspoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
50 g dried red bird's-eye chiles, for the chili paste
100 g fresh red chiles, chopped, for the chili paste
1 tablespoon black peppercorns, for the chili paste
5-7 lemongrass stalks, chopped, for the chili paste
1 × 4 cm piece galangal, peeled and chopped, for the chili paste
3 tablespoons turmeric, for the chili paste
1 garlic bulb, cloves separated and chopped, for the chili paste

Season with the fish sauce and sugar, stir, and add the kaffir lime leaves and green peppercorns. Stir-fry for 1-2 minutes. Serve.

recipes.title: Roasted Duck Curry
recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 red spur chile, diagonally sliced, to garnish

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Pound the garlic and cilantro (coriander) root in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the curry paste, pound again until thoroughly combined, and set aside.

Add the pineapple, tomatoes, duck, grapes, and remaining coconut milk and stir. Add both ground seeds, the kaffir lime leaf, and red chile, reduce the heat, and simmer for about 3 minutes, Season with the fish sauce and sugar, add the basil leaves, and stir. Garnish with the sliced red chile and a swirl of coconut cream. Serve.

recipes.title: Roasted Duck Curry with Lychee
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 21⁄2 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
100 g cubed pineapple, cut into 3 cm cubes
10 lychees or rambutans, peeled and pitted sweet basil leaves, to garnish
1 red spur chile, finely sliced, to garnish Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Put the duck breast in a shallow dish and rub the soy sauce all over the meat, then let marinate for 5-10 minutes.

Add the duck and broth (stock) and boil for another 3-4 minutes, then add the fish sauce sugar, round and pea eggplants (aubergines), pineapple, kaffir lime leaves, and lychees or rambutans. Boil for another 4-5 minutes, then garnish with basil leaves and the red chile and serve with rice.

recipes.title: Chicken Curry with Herbs
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 700 g boneless chicken thighs, cut into small pieces
1 red spur chile Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the curry paste and sauté for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir-fry for 4-5 minutes. Carefully pour in the water and cook for another 10 minutes, until the chicken is cooked. Season with the salt.
Add the cardamom shoots and pea eggplants and cook for 2 minutes. Add the kaffir lime leaves and both chiles and cook for another 2 minutes.
Fill a small bowl to the rim with steamed rice and invert it in the middle of a serving plate. Serve with the curry.

recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 400 g boneless chicken thighs, cut into 3 cm cubes
1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
100 g round eggplants (aubergines), cut into quarters
1 red spur chile, diagonally sliced Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over low-medium heat, add the curry paste, and stir-fry for about 2 minutes until sizzling and fragrant. Add the chicken and cook for 1-2 minutes. Pour in half the coconut milk, stir well, then increase the heat to medium and cook for 2-3 minutes. Add the remaining coconut milk, the fish sauce, and sugar and stir again. Add both eggplants (aubergines), then cover the wok and let boil for 4-5 minutes until the eggplants are cooked. Add the basil leaves and chile, stir for 30 seconds, then transfer to a serving bowl. Garnish with basil leaves and sliced chiles and serve with rice.

recipes.title: Spicy Chicken Curry
recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 500 g chicken thighs, boned and cut into small pieces
1 x 4 cm piece galangal, peeled and sliced
65 g pennywort or watercress (optional) Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring the broth to a boil in a large pan. Add the chili paste and return to a boil for 2-3 minutes.
Add the chicken and boil for another 4-5 minutes.
Add the galangal, fish sauce, sugar, and salt and return to a boil for 5-8 minutes, until the chicken is cooked and fully flavored.
Add the kaffir lime leaves and pennywort or watercress and cook for another minute. Serve with rice.

Add the kaffir lime leaves and pennywort or watercress and cook for another minute. Serve with rice.

recipes.title: Spicy Chicken Curry and Young Banana
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 tablespoon granulated sugar Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve

ingredientGroups.heading: For the chili paste
lines: 20 red and green bird's-eye chiles, chopped

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the chili paste, pound all its ingredients together in a mortar with a pestle until smooth.
Dissolve the salt in the water. Wash the peeled bananas in the salt water, then cut them into 3 cm-thick slices.
Heat the coconut cream in a wok over medium heat. Add the chili paste, chicken, bananas, and coconut milk and simmer for about 10 minutes, until the chicken and bananas are cooked.
Season with the fish sauce and sugar, garnish with the chile and basil, and serve with rice.

recipes.title: Chicken and Bitter Gourd Curry Soup with Noodles
recipes.subtitle: Central

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the dried noodles in a bowl of water for 10 minutes or prepare according to package directions. Drain and set aside.

Cook the chicken in a pan of boiling water over medium heat for 4-5 minutes or until cooked. Remove with a slotted spoon and shred into bite-size pieces with a fork. Set aside. For the curry soup, bring the broth (stock) to a boil in a large pan over medium heat and add the remaining ingredients except for the bitter gourd and boil for about 5 minutes. Add the bitter gourd, return to a boil, and cook for another 5 minutes. Reduce the heat to low and let simmer for 30 minutes.

Blanch the bean sprouts in a pan of boiling water for 1-2 minutes, then drain, add to the noodles, and divide among serving bowls. Add the shredded chicken, pork blood curd, cilantro (coriander), and scallions (spring onions), then pour the soup into the bowls and serve.

recipes.title: Spicy Chicken Curry with Bamboo Shoots
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 4-5 orange and red spur chiles, chopped
200 g boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into bite-size pieces
1 red spur chile, diagonally sliced, to garnish Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Pound the chiles and garlic together in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the chile-garlic mixture, and saute for 1 minute or until fragrant. Add the chicken and stir-fry for 3-4 minutes or until the chicken is cooked. Add the bamboo shoots and stir-fry for another 1 minute. Season with the fish sauce, sugar, and kaffir lime leaves and stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until thoroughly combined, Garnish with the basil leaves and sliced red chile, and serve with rice.

recipes.searchText: Spicy Chicken Curry with Bamboo Shoots Central 4-5 orange and red spur chiles, chopped 4-5 cloves garlic, chopped 2 tablespoons vegetable oil 200 g boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into bite-size pieces 300 g sliced bamboo shoot strips 2 tablespoons fish sauce 1 teaspoon granulated sugar 4-5 kaffir lime leaves, torn 1 handful of holy basil leaves 1 red spur chile, diagonally sliced, to garnish Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve Pound the chiles and garlic together in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the bamboo shoots and stir-fry for another 1 minute. Season with the fish sauce, sugar, and kaffir lime leaves and stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until thoroughly combined, Garnish with the basil leaves and sliced red chile, and serve with rice.

recipes.title: Chicken Curry with Yellow Glutinous Rice
recipes.subtitle: North
recipes.prepTime: 15–30 minutes, plus soaking and marinating time

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 500 g boneless chicken thigh, cut into 4 cm pieces
3 tablespoons Fried Shallots (see p. 64), plus their oil, to garnish

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the glutinous rice in water with the turmeric overnight, then drain. Wrap the rice in cheesecloth and steam for 30-35 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes, until cooked and translucent. Keep covered.
For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in warm water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.
Preheat the broiler to medium. Broil the soybean sheet for 1-2 minutes, until fragrant and dark brown, then let cool.
Pound the chiles and salt in a mortar with a pestle. Add the soybean sheet, lemongrass, shallots, garlic, and shrimp paste and pound until smooth.
Mix the chicken with the chili paste, cover, and marinate in the refrigerator for 15-30 minutes.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the chicken and cook for 6-7 minutes, until it begins to brown. Carefully add the water, tomatoes, and salt and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer for 40-50 minutes, until the chicken is tender and the liquid has reduced by one-third.
Pour the fried shallot oil over the yellow glutinous rice, sprinkle with the fried shallots, and serve with the curry.

recipes.title: Green Curry with Silkworm Pupae
recipes.subtitle: Northeast

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 2 long eggplants (aubergines), sliced into 2.5 cm pieces

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Blanch the silkworm pupae in a pan of boiling water for 1 minute. Drain, transfer to a heatproof bowl, add the fish sauce, and marinate for 10 minutes.
Bring the coconut milk to a boil over medium heat, add the curry paste, and return to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer for about 2 minutes, until fragrant.
Add the pupae and eggplants and return to a boil. Cook for 5-7 minutes. Add the chile, basil, and kaffir lime leaves, stir, and serve.

recipes.title: Sour Horse Mango Curry
recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 2 x T 200 g mackerel, sliced into bite-size pieces
1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in a bowl of warm water for 15 minutes or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.
Pound the dried chiles, salt, shallots, and the shrimp paste in a mortar with a pestle until smooth, then set aside.
Dissolve the salt in 475 ml water. Soak the horse mangoes in the salt water for 5 minutes, then drain.

Bring 750 ml water to a boil in a pan over medium heat. Add the paste, stir, and return to a boil. Add the mackerel and horse mango and cook for 6-8 minutes. Add the sugar and stir until dissolved. Serve.

recipes.title: Corn Curry in Banana Leaves
recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 40 g grated fresh coconut or dry unsweetened desiccated coconut Pinch of salt

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Preheat a charcoal or gas grill to 200°C.
Pound the fingerroot in a mortar. Add the curry paste and pound until smooth, then add the corn, coconut, and salt and pound until the mixture becomes sticky.
Layer the banana leaves back to back with their shiny sides facing outward. Put the curry mixture in the center and flatten it slightly. Fold in the sides and ends and secure with a toothpick.
Grill over low heat for 8 minutes on each side, until cooked. Unwrap and serve.

recipes.title: Steamed Mushroom Curry in Banana Leaves
recipes.subtitle: Northeast

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 150 g mushrooms, such as white beach, cleaned and stems removed
2 banana leaf sheets, about 8 x 9 inches/20 x 23 cm

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Mix the mushrooms, egg, lemongrass, basil leaves, chiles, and shallot together in a bowl. Add the fish sauce and fermented fish sauce and mix again.

Place the 2 banana leaf sheets back to back on a work surface with the shiny surface face outward on both sides. Put the mushroom mixture in the center of the banana leaf sheets and flatten the mixture slightly to make it easy to wrap. Cover the curry with the sides of the sheets, fold over the ends, and secure with a toothpick Steam the banana-leaf package in a steamer over medium heat for 15 minutes or until cooked. Unwrap and serve.

recipes.title: Coconut Curry with Wax Gourd and Noodles
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 300 g wax gourd, peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes
1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the noodles in water for 10 minutes, or prepare according to package directions, then drain.
Pound the shallots, peppercorns, salt, and shrimp paste in a mortar until smooth.
Bring the coconut milk to a boil in a pan over medium heat. Add the paste and boil for about 2 minutes, until fragrant.
Add the wax gourd and sugar and cook for 12 minutes, until the gourd is tender and flavored.
Add the drained noodles and cook for another 1-2 minutes, until soft. Serve.

recipes.title: Spicy-and-Sour Curry with Durian and Shrimp
recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 2 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
300 g durian flesh, cut into bite-size pieces
200 g uncooked shrimp, peeled and deveined, tails intact
10 fresh red and green bird's-eye chiles

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the curry paste, soak the dried chiles in warm water for 15 minutes, then drain and chop.
Pound the rehydrated and fresh chiles with the shallots and turmeric until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and salt and pound until combined.
Bring 600 ml water to a boil over medium-high heat. Add the curry paste, sugar, fish sauce, tamarind puree, lime juice, durian, and shrimp.
Return to a boil and cook for 10 minutes. Serve.

recipes.title: Durian Massaman Curry
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 500 g boneless chicken, cut into 5 cm pieces
3 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar

ingredientGroups.heading: For the massaman chili paste
lines: 1 teaspoon shrimp paste Pickled ginger, pickled cucumber, and salad greens, to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in warm water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain and chop. Pound with the remaining chili paste ingredients in a mortar until smooth.
Dry-fry the peanuts, coriander, tree basil, cloves, cardamom, and cinnamon in a wok for 1 minute, until fragrant. Set aside.
Bring the coconut milk to a simmer in a clean wok over low heat, stirring continuously, until grainy.
Add the chili paste and stir for 1-2 minutes, until fragrant. Add the chicken, roasted spices, fish sauce, bay leaves, tamarind, and sugar and cook for 20-25 minutes.
Add the durian and cook for 5 minutes. Serve with pickled ginger, pickled cucumber, and salad greens.

recipes.title: Spicy Taro Stem Curry
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 × 800 g snakehead fish, cleaned and descaled
1 kg fresh taro stems, washed and cut into 5 cm pieces
300 g pork belly, cut into 2.5 cm pieces
2 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
25 g ground dried red chiles, for the chili paste
1 × 4 cm piece galangal, peeled and chopped, for the chili paste
1 garlic bulb, cloves separated and chopped, for the chili paste
1 shallot, chopped, for the chili paste
40 g chopped fingerroot, for the chili paste
20 g chopped lemongrass, for the chili paste

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Preheat the boiler (grill) to medium-high, place the fish on the broiler (grill) rack, and broil (grill) for 10-12 minutes on each side. Remove the meat and discard the skin and bones. Set aside.

For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in a bowl of warm water for 15 minutes or until rehydrated, then drain and chop. Pound the chiles, galangal, garlic, shallot, fingerroot, and lemongrass in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the grilled fish meat and pound again, then set aside.
Bring a large pan of water to a boil over medium heat. Add the taro stems and boil for 5-7 minutes or until softened. Drain, squeeze to remove any excess liquid, and set aside.

Bring the coconut milk, chili paste, and fermented fish to a boil in a pan over medium heat. Add the pork and return to a boil. Add the taro stems, reduce the heat, and simmer for 5 minutes or until cooked. Add the fish sauce, sugar, tamarind, and kaffir lime leaves and serve.

recipes.title: Spicy Banana Blossom Curry
recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 2 x 400 g mackerel, cleaned, filleted, and sliced into bite-size pieces

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the chilli paste, pound all the ingredients together in a mortar with a pestle until smooth Set aside To clean and prepare banana blossom, pour 475 ml water into a large bowl, add the salt, and stir until dissolved. Peel away and discard the outer red petals from the banana blossom and also the small white strips of banana flower. Cut off the tip and the end of the blossom, then cut the blossom crosswise into thin slices. Put the slices into the bowl of water and let soak for 10 minutes, then drain and set aside.

Bring a large pan of water to a boil over medium heat, add the chili paste and banana blossom, stir, and return to a boil. Add the mackerel, then return to a boil and cook for about 3 minutes. Add the sweet basil leaves and stir. Serve.
