Bring a large pan of water to a boil over medium heat, add the chili paste and banana blossom, stir, and return to a boil. Add the mackerel, then return to a boil and cook for about 3 minutes. Add the sweet basil leaves and stir. Serve.

recipes.title: Sweet Taro Stem Curry
recipes.subtitle: Northeast

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 3 taro stems, washed, peeled, and cut into large pieces

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Preheat a charcoal or gas grill to 200°C, or preheat an indoor broiler to medium. Grill or broil the pork for 7-8 minutes on each side, until cooked. Slice into bite-size pieces.
Boil the taro stems for 5-7 minutes, until softened. Drain and squeeze out any excess liquid.
Bring the coconut milk to a boil in a wok over medium heat. Add the chili paste and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes, until fragrant.
Add the pork and season with the sugar, tamarind, fish sauce, and fermented fish sauce. Return to a boil.
Add the taro stems and the acacia leaves, if using. Return to a boil and cook for about 5 minutes. Serve.

recipes.searchText: Sweet Taro Stem Curry Northeast 300 g pork loin 3 taro stems, washed, peeled, and cut into large pieces 250 ml coconut milk 100 g chili paste 1 teaspoon granulated sugar 1 teaspoon Tamarind Puree (see p. 63) 1 teaspoon fish sauce 2 teaspoons fermented fish sauce 3-5 acacia leaves (optional) Preheat a charcoal or gas grill to 200°C, or preheat an indoor broiler to medium. Grill or broil the pork for 7-8 minutes on each side, until cooked. Slice into bite-size pieces. Boil the taro stems for 5-7 minutes, until softened. Drain and squeeze out any excess liquid. Bring the coconut milk to a boil in a wok over medium heat. Add the chili paste and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes, until fragrant. Add the pork and season with the sugar, tamarind, fish sauce, and fermented fish sauce. Return to a boil. Add the taro stems and the acacia leaves, if using. Return to a boil and cook for about 5 minutes. Serve.

Grill over high heat for 6-7 minutes on each side. If broiling, position the rack about 10 cm from the heat and broil for 6-7 minutes on each side.
Slice the squid into small rings and serve with Seafood Dipping Sauce.

ingredientGroups.heading: For the dipping sauce
lines: 21⁄2 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
3 red and green bird's-eye chiles, chopped

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Prepare a charcoal or gas grill for 350°F/180°C, or preheat an indoor broiler to medium.
For the dipping sauce, bring the tamarind and sugar to a boil in a pan over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Let cool, then add the chiles, shallots, and salt.

Grill over medium heat for 7-8 minutes on each side, until cooked. If broiling, position the rack about 10 cm from the heat and broil for 7-8 minutes on each side, turning occasionally.
Unwrap the fish and serve with the dipping sauce.

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 2-3 lemongrass stalks, chopped and lightly pounded
130 g salt flakes raw vegetables, such as cabbage, lettuce, galangal, ginger, garlic, and round eggplant, to serve fresh herbs, such as dill and cilantro (coriander), to serve

ingredientGroups.heading: For the spicy fermented fish dip
For the spicy seafood dip
lines: 2 garlic bulbs, cloves separated and peeled

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: To make the fermented fish dip, dry-fry the shallots, garlic, galangal, and lemongrass in a wok for 2-3 minutes or until fragrant. Let cool slightly, then peel. Transfer to a mortar, add the chili flakes, and finely pound with a pestle. Add the fermented fish, then pound thoroughly until combined. Set aside.
For the spicy seafood dip, finely pound the chiles, garlic, and salt together in a mortar with a pestle. Add the fish sauce and sugar and stir Set aside.
For the spicy tamarind dip, finely pound the chiles, garlic, and salt together in a mortar with a pestle. Add the tamarind and sugar and stir Set aside.

Before you begin cooking, check that your charcoal is glowing white hot, or your gas grill (barbecue) is preheated to 400°F/200°C. Alternatively, use a conventional indoor broiler (grill) preheated to medium. Stuff the lemongrass into the fish cavity and rub both sides of the fish with the salt.

Grill the fish over medium heat for about 10 minutes on each side or until cooked. If using an indoor broiler, put the broiler (grill) rack 10 cm away from the heat source, then place the fish on the rack and broil (grill) for about 10 minutes on each side or until cooked.

Grill over medium heat for 15 minutes on each side, until cooked. If broiling, place the fish on a broiler rack and cook over medium heat for 15 minutes on each side.

lines: 4 cm piece turmeric root, peeled and chopped
2 cm piece galangal, peeled and chopped
500 g snakehead fish, cleaned and descaled
To serve Tomato Chili Sauce (see p. 64), Barbecue Sauce (see p. 63), or Seafood Dipping Sauce (see p. 58) raw or steamed vegetables, such as cucumber, napa cabbage, and small bitter gourd

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Heat a charcoal or gas grill to 400°F/200°C, or preheat the oven to 325°F/160°C/Gas Mark 3.
Soak the dried chiles in warm water for 15 minutes, then drain and chop. Pound the chiles, turmeric, galangal, shallots, lemongrass, and salt until smooth. Rub the paste over the whole fish.
Push the basil into the bamboo, followed by the fish. Roast on the grill or in the oven for about 30 minutes, rotating the bamboo regularly.
Remove from the heat, break open the bamboo, and serve with a sauce and raw or steamed vegetables.

recipes.title: Catfish and Neem with Sweet Sauce
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 2 lemongrass stalks, finely sliced and pounded
10-15 dried red chiles, fried, to serve Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve

ingredientGroups.heading: For the sweet sauce
lines: 41⁄2 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
11⁄2 tablespoons fish sauce A pinch of salt

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Score the fish 2-3 times on each side.
Mix the lemongrass, black pepper, cilantro roots, and soy sauce. Rub the mixture over the fish and inside its cavity.

Prepare a grill for 400°F/200°C. Cook the fish over medium heat for 10-15 minutes on each side. Alternatively, broil it 7 cm from a medium-high heat source for 13-15 minutes on each side, until the skin is dry and brown and the fish is cooked.
For the sauce, combine the sugar, tamarind, fish sauce, salt, and 1-2 tablespoons water in a wok over medium heat. Stir for 4-5 minutes, until thickened, then add the fried shallots.
Blanch the neem in hot water 2-3 times, then drain and refresh in cold water.
Serve portions of neem, fish, fried chile, and sweet sauce together with rice.

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 6 kaffir lime leaves, finely sliced Glutinous Rice (see p. 378), to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in warm water for 15 minutes, or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.
Pound the chiles and salt in a mortar with a pestle. Add the lemongrass, turmeric, garlic, and shallot and pound until smooth. Add the shrimp paste and pound until thoroughly combined.
Turn the casings inside out and soak in the water mixed with 11⁄2 tablespoons salt for about 10 minutes. Drain and turn right-side out.
Mix the pork and chili paste in a large bowl. Add both cilantro, scallions, kaffir lime leaves, and the remaining teaspoon salt and mix well.
Prepare a grill for 400°F/200°C, or preheat an indoor broiler to medium-high.
Fill the casings with the pork mixture using a sausage funnel, tie both ends, and prick the sausages with a toothpick.
Grill over medium heat for 15-18 minutes on each side, until browned and cooked. If broiling, position the rack 10 cm from the heat and broil for about 15 minutes on each side.
Slice diagonally and serve with glutinous rice.

lines: 2 cups (16 fl oz/475 mil) vegetable oil

ingredientGroups.heading: For the tamarind sauce
lines: 3 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the kale leaves, and fry for 1 minute or until the kale starts to become crispy. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Put the duck, soy sauce, white pepper, and five-spice powder in a bowl and mix well. Cover with plastic wrap (clingfilm) and let marinate in the refrigerator for 20 minutes. Preheat a grill pan (griddle) over high heat. Place the duck, skin side down, in the pan, then reduce the heat to low and grill for 7 minutes or until brown and crispy. Turn over and grill for 10 minutes. Remove and set aside.
For the sauce, heat the sugar, tamarind, soy sauce, and 1 tablespoon water together in a pan over medium-low heat. Cook for 5-6 minutes or until thickened. Set aside.

Carve the duck breast into 1 cm-thick pieces and place on a serving plate with the pieces overlapping in a fan shape. Put the crispy kale to one side of the duck and pour over the sauce. Sprinkle with the fried garlic, fried shallots, roasted chile, and cilantro (coriander) leaves and serve.

Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Put the duck, soy sauce, white pepper, and five-spice powder in a bowl and mix well. Cover with plastic wrap (clingfilm) and let marinate in the refrigerator for 20 minutes. Preheat a grill pan (griddle) over high heat. Place the duck, skin side down, in the pan, then reduce the heat to low and grill for 7 minutes or until brown and crispy. Turn over and grill for 10 minutes. Remove and set aside. For the sauce, heat the sugar, tamarind, soy sauce, and 1 tablespoon water together in a pan over medium-low heat. Cook for 5-6 minutes or until thickened. Set aside. Carve the duck breast into 1 cm-thick pieces and place on a serving plate with the pieces overlapping in a fan shape. Put the crispy kale to one side of the duck and pour over the sauce. Sprinkle with the fried garlic, fried shallots, roasted chile, and cilantro (coriander) leaves and serve.

recipes.title: Grilled Pork Salad
recipes.subtitle: North

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 400 g skinless pork neck, fillet, or shoulder
10 dried red chiles, seeded and chopped
2 tablespoons fish sauce Glutinous Rice (see p. 378), to serve Raw vegetables, such as carrots, cucumbers, and Chinese greens, to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Preheat a charcoal or gas grill to 160°C, or preheat an indoor broiler to medium-low.
Rub the soy sauce over the pork, cover, and marinate for 15 minutes.
Grill the pork over medium-low heat for 15-20 minutes on each side, until browned and cooked. If broiling, position the rack about 10 cm from the heat and broil for 15-20 minutes on each side.
Shred the cooked pork with a fork, then pound it briefly in a mortar.
Transfer the pork to a bowl. Add the garlic, shallots, lemongrass, chiles, lemon juice, and fish sauce and mix well.
Serve with glutinous rice and raw vegetables.

recipes.title: Stewed Pork Side
recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 500 g pork side (belly), cut into 5 cm cubes
120 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
475 ml water, plus more if needed
4 hard-boiled eggs Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Heat the oil in a pan or casserole over medium heat. Add the saam-gler and sauté for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the pork and cook for about 4 minutes, until golden brown.
Add the water, sugar, both soy sauces, five-spice powder, and black pepper. Mix well and return to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 30 minutes.
Add the eggs and partially cover with a lid. Simmer for 1 hour, until the pork is tender, stirring occasionally and adding water if needed to prevent the meat from drying out. Serve with rice.

recipes.title: Stewed Pork with Peanuts and Dried Bamboo Shoots
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 kg pork side (belly), diced with the fat
200 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar

ingredientGroups.heading: For the chili paste
lines: 1 medium garlic bulb, cloves separated and chopped
1 x 12.5 cm piece galangal, peeled and chopped

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the bamboo shoots in water for 15 minutes, then drain. Cut into 7.5 cm segments.
Cook the peanuts in boiling water for about 5 minutes, until soft, then drain.
For the chili paste, pound all its ingredients together in a mortar with a pestle until smooth.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the chili paste and stir-fry for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the pork, peanuts, bamboo shoots, sugar, and fish sauce and stir-fry for 5-6 minutes, until cooked. Serve.

Add the pork, peanuts, bamboo shoots, sugar, and fish sauce and stir-fry for 5-6 minutes, until cooked. Serve.

recipes.title: Steamed Sea Bass with Spicy Lime Sauce
recipes.subtitle: North

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 × 800 g whole sea bass, cleaned and filleted
3-4 red and green bird's-eye chiles, chopped, for the sauce
4 garlic cloves, chopped, for the sauce
11⁄2 teaspoons chopped cilantro root, for the sauce
60 ml chicken broth, for the sauce
3 tablespoons fish sauce, for the sauce
2 tablespoons lime juice, for the sauce
1 tablespoon granulated sugar, for the sauce
1 small handful cilantro sprigs, to garnish
3 red bird's-eye chiles, sliced, to garnish

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the sauce, pound the chiles, garlic, and cilantro (coriander) root in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Transfer to a bowl. Add the chicken broth (stock), fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, and 60 ml water and stir until thoroughly combined. Place one of the fillets, skin side down, in a deep plate. Cover with the galangal and half the lemongrass, then put the remaining fillet on top, skin side up. Arrange the kaffir lime leaves and the remaining lemongrass around the fillets. Steam in a steamer for 5-7 minutes, then pour over the sauce and steam for another 5 minutes or until the fish is cooked through. Transfer to a shallow serving bowl. Garnish with sliced lime, cilantro (coriander) sprigs, and chile and serve.

recipes.title: Steamed Tilapia with Spicy Tomato Dip
recipes.subtitle: North

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 2-3 lemongrass stalks, chopped and lightly pounded
10 kaffir lime leaves, plus a few extra
2 tablespoons coarse sea salt Raw vegetables, such as cabbage, snake gourd, and napa cabbage, to serve Vegetable hummingbird and Chinese mustard flowers, coarsely chopped, to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the dip, roast the tomato, chiles, and shallots in a dry skillet over low heat for 2-3 minutes, until fragrant.
Lightly pound the chiles and shallots in a mortar. Add the tomato and pound again, then mix in the salt and tamarind puree. Sprinkle with cilantro.
Score the tilapia 2-3 times on both sides. Stuff the lemongrass, galangal, and kaffir lime leaves into the cavity.
Season both sides generously with sea salt and tuck a few extra kaffir lime leaves into the score marks.
Steam the fish for about 20 minutes. In a separate steamer, steam the vegetables and flowers for about 10 minutes.
Serve the fish with the vegetables, flowers, and spicy tomato dip.

recipes.title: Steamed Catfish in Banana Leaf
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: Banana leaves, cut into circles about 20 cm in diameter
250 g snakehead fish fillet, cut into 2.5 cm cubes
15 g finely sliced kaffir lime leaves
15 g finely sliced great morinda leaves or sweet basil leaves
1 red spur chile, finely sliced lengthwise, to garnish

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For each cup, place 2 banana-leaf circles back to back, shiny sides facing outward. Fold up a 5 cm section and fold it in on itself to form a corner; secure with a toothpick. Repeat to make 4 corners.
Whisk the coconut cream and curry paste in a large bowl until the paste dissolves. Add the eggs, oyster sauce, fish sauce, and sugar and whisk until combined.
Add the fish, kaffir lime leaves, and morinda or basil leaves and mix gently.
Fill the banana cups with the mixture, making sure each contains at least 4-5 pieces of fish.
Steam over medium-high heat for 20-25 minutes, until the mixture has set and feels firm. Garnish each cup with red chile and serve.

recipes.title: Steamed Fish with Pumpkin and Herbs
recipes.subtitle: Northeast

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 2 lemongrass stalks, halved crosswise and crushed
200 g pumpkin wedge, cut into 3-4 pieces
1 handful basil or Greek basil, to garnish Spicy Tomato Dip (see p. 54) or Seafood Dipping Sauce (see p. 58), to serve Glutinous Rice (see p. 378), to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Rinse the fish in cold water, pat dry with paper towels, then rub the whole fish with the salt and set aside, Coarsely pound the shallots, garlic, black peppercorns, and cilantro (coriander) root together in a mortar with a pestle. Add the soy sauce and stuff the mixture inside the fish cavity. Put the lemongrass and galangal in the center of a large heatproof plate, then place the fish on the top. Arrange the pumpkin around the fish and steam in a steamer for about 15 minutes or until the fish is cooked. Garnish with the basil and serve with rice and spicy tomato dip or seafood sauce.

recipes.title: Steamed Egg with Shrimp and Coconut Milk
recipes.subtitle: South

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 tablespoon salted tiny freshwater shrimp or 11⁄2 teaspoons shrimp paste mixed with 1 tablespoon water
1 shallot, sliced red and green bird's eye chiles, sliced, to garnish

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Beat the eggs and coconut milk in a large bowl, then add the shrimp and shallot and beat again until thoroughly combined. Let sit for about 2 minutes to let the air bubbles dissipate. Pour the mixture into small heatproof cups and steam in a steamer over medium heat for 15-20 minutes or until cooked. To see if the eggs are cooked, push a skewer through the center-only clear water should come out. Sprinkle with the chiles and serve.

Let sit for about 2 minutes to let the air bubbles dissipate. Pour the mixture into small heatproof cups and steam in a steamer over medium heat for 15-20 minutes or until cooked. recipes.title: Steamed Egg with Shrimp and Mushrooms
recipes.subtitle: Central

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the mushrooms in a bowl of boiling water for 15 minutes, then drain, slice, and set aside. Pour the broth (stock) or water into a large bowl, add the eggs, mushrooms, shrimp, fish sauce, and soy sauce, and beat until thoroughly combined. Let sit for about 2 minutes to let the air bubbles dissipate.

Pour the mixture into a small heatproof bowl and steam in a steamer over medium heat for 15-20 minutes or until cooked. To see if the eggs are cooked, push a skewer through the center-only clear water should come out. Serve sprinkled with the carrot, onion, and scallion (spring onion).

recipes.searchText: Steamed Egg with Shrimp and Mushrooms Central 4 dried shiitake mushrooms 120 ml chicken broth (stock) or water 4-5 eggs, beaten 6-8 shrimp (prawns), peeled, deveined, and chopped 1⁄2 teaspoon fish sauce 2 teaspoons soy sauce 1 small carrot, finely shredded 1 onion, finely chopped 1 tablespoon sliced scallion (spring onion) Soak the mushrooms in a bowl of boiling water for 15 minutes, then drain, slice, and set aside. recipes.title: Stuffed Mangrove Trumpet Tree Flowers
recipes.subtitle: Northeast

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 4 lemongrass stalks, sliced 50 g bird's eye chiles
500 g clown featherback or flounder fillet, finely chopped
30 g kaffir lime leaves, finely sliced, plus whole ones to garnish
20 mangrove trumpet tree flowers or zucchini (courgette) flowers

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Put the glutinous (sticky) rice in a large bowl, add 120 ml water, and let soak for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally. Drain and reserve the rice water.

Pound the lemongrass, chiles, salt, and glutinous rice water in a mortar with a pestle. Add the fish, pork, and fermented fish sauce and pound thoroughly. Add the dill and kaffir lime leaves, then pound again until smooth. Spoon the paste into the flowers and place on cheesecloth (muslin) in a steamer. Steam for about 30 minutes. Serve garnished with kaffir lime leaves.

recipes.searchText: Stuffed Mangrove Trumpet Tree Flowers Northeast 100 g uncooked glutinous (sticky) rice 4 lemongrass stalks, sliced 50 g bird's eye chiles 1 teaspoon salt 500 g clown featherback or flounder fillet, finely chopped 200 g ground (minced) pork 2 tablespoons fermented fish sauce 80 g chopped dill 30 g kaffir lime leaves, finely sliced, plus whole ones to garnish 20 mangrove trumpet tree flowers or zucchini (courgette) flowers Put the glutinous (sticky) rice in a large bowl, add 120 ml water, and let soak for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally. recipes.title: Stuffed Squid with Garlic and Pepper
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 400 g small squid, cleaned, with tentacles intact

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Mix the ground (minced) pork with 1 tablespoon soy sauce, the salt, sugar, and 11⁄2 teaspoons Saam-Gler in a large bowl until thoroughly combined. Stuff the squid with the pork mixture until three-quarters full. Thread the sides of the squid together, using a toothpick or skewer. Steam the stuffed squid in a steamer over medium heat for 10-12 minutes or until cooked. Remove and set aside.

Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the remaining saam-gler, and stir-fry for 1 minute or until fragrant. Add the steamed squid and remaining soy sauce, then stir-fry for another 1-2 minutes or until the squid is well coated with the saam-gler. Serve sprinkled with the cilantro (coriander).

recipes.title: Steamed Pork Patties with Salted Egg
recipes.subtitle: Central

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Finely pound the cilantro (coriander) root, garlic, and white peppercorns together in a mortar with a pestle. Put the ground (minced) pork, salted egg whites, soy sauce, sesame oil, and the cilantro root paste in a large bowl and mix well. Mold the pork mixture into flat round patties, 10 cm in diameter. Lightly press a piece of salted egg yolk into the center of each patty. Arrange the patties in a shallow dish and steam in a steamer for 15-20 minutes over medium heat until cooked. Serve.

recipes.title: Sweet Boiled Mackerel
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 5-7.5 cm piece fresh ginger, peeled and pounded
2 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring a large pan of water to a boil, then add all the ingredients, reduce the heat to low, and simmer for 20 minutes. Serve hot or cold.

recipes.searchText: Sweet Boiled Mackerel Central 5 small mackerel, cleaned and descaled 5 cloves garlic, pounded 5-7.5 cm piece fresh ginger, peeled and pounded 2 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar 1 tablespoon Tamarind Puree (see p. 63) 1 teaspoon salt Bring a large pan of water to a boil, then add all the ingredients, reduce the heat to low, and simmer for 20 minutes. Serve hot or cold.

recipes.title: Bilimbi with Dipping Sauce
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: For the dipping sauce
lines: 80 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the dipping sauce, put the shrimp paste, sugar, and 120 ml water in a pan over medium heat, stir, and cook for 3-4 minutes. Remove from heat and let cool. Add the chiles and shallots, stir well, then transfer to a small serving bowl.
Arrange the sliced bilimbi on a serving plate and serve with the dipping sauce on the side.

recipes.searchText: Bilimbi with Dipping Sauce Central 30 bilimbi, sliced 30 g shrimp paste 80 g jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar 5 red bird's eye chiles, chopped 2 shallots, sliced For the dipping sauce, put the shrimp paste, sugar, and 120 ml water in a pan over medium heat, stir, and cook for 3-4 minutes. Remove from heat and let cool. Add the chiles and shallots, stir well, then transfer to a small serving bowl. Arrange the sliced bilimbi on a serving plate and serve with the dipping sauce on the side.

recipes.title: Slow-Cooked Mackerel
recipes.subtitle: Northeast

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 2.5 cm piece galangal, peeled and chopped
10 cm piece sugar cane, quartered lengthwise
300 g pork side (belly), cut into 1 cm dice
1 kg horse mackerel, cleaned and heads removed
2 tablespoons dark soy sauce Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Put the galangal, lemongrass, and half the sugar cane in a large, deep pan. Place the pork and mackerel on top and add enough water to cover the fish. Do not stir from this point.

Pound the shallot, garlic, and salt and add to the pan with the sugar, fish sauce, and soy sauce. Put the remaining sugar cane on top of the fish and bring to a boil over medium heat. Cook for 30 minutes and skim.

Reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 3-4 hours, or until the fish is cooked and its bones have softened. Add more water if the liquid dries out and stir gently only if necessary. Serve with rice.

recipes.title: Sweet Boiled Shrimp
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 teaspoon salt Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring 120 ml water to a boil in a large pan, add the shrimp (prawns), sugar, and salt, and mix well. Reduce the heat and simmer for 7-8 minutes or until the water has evaporated. Let cool, then serve with the rice.

recipes.searchText: Sweet Boiled Shrimp Central 500 g uncooked shrimp (prawns) 150 g superfine (caster) sugar 1 teaspoon salt Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve Bring 120 ml water to a boil in a large pan, add the shrimp (prawns), sugar, and salt, and mix well. recipes.title: Pork and Herb Meatballs
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 x 2 cm piece fresh ginger, peeled and finely chopped
1 teaspoon salt Vegetable oil, for frying Glutinous Rice (see p. 378), to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Combine the pork, tomatoes, shallots, both cilantro, garlic, ginger, lemongrass, scallions, turmeric, and salt in a large bowl.
With damp hands, roll the mixture into 5 cm-diameter balls.
Heat a layer of oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Sauté the meatballs in batches for 6-7 minutes, until well browned all over.
Transfer to a serving plate and serve with glutinous rice.

lines: 1 x 1.3 kg chicken, chopped into pieces

steps: For the paste, pound the galangal, lemongrass, shallots, ginger, cilantro roots, garlic, kaffir lime leaves, salt, black pepper, and soy sauce in a mortar with a pestle until smooth.

steps: Soak the dried chiles in a bowl of warm water for 15 minutes or until rehydrated, then drain and chop. Pound the chiles, shallots, and shrimp paste in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. steps: Cut the pumpkin into 1 x 2.5 cm sticks, rinse under cold running water, and set aside.
Bring the coconut milk and pumpkin sticks to a boil in a pan over medium heat. Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer for about 10 minutes, until the pumpkin has softened.
Add both sugars and the salt and return to a boil. Add the coconut cream, bring back to a boil, then remove from the heat and serve.

recipes.title: Water Spinach with Shrimp and Tofu

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 150 g extra-firm tofu, cut into cubes
8 raw freshwater shrimp, heads and tails intact
3-5 dried red chiles, finely pounded, for the sauce

3 tablespoons white vinegar, for the sauce
3 tablespoons granulated sugar, for the sauce
3 tablespoons fish sauce, for the sauce

steps: Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Stir-fry the tofu for 5-7 minutes, until golden brown. Remove with a slotted spoon and set aside.

Put all the sauce ingredients in a pan over medium heat and simmer until thick.
Blanch the water spinach in boiling water for 1 minute, then drain.
Arrange the cucumber on a serving plate and cover with the water spinach. Drizzle with the sauce and sprinkle with the sesame seeds, peanuts, and fried garlic. Top with the tofu and shrimp and serve.

Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Fry the mackerel until browned and the skin is crisp, turning to cook both sides.

steps: Heat the oil for deep-frying in a wok or deep fryer to 350°F/180°C or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds. Deep-fry the fish for 8-10 minutes or until golden and crispy. recipes.title: Fried Sea Bass

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 80 g green sour mango, peeled and julienned
1 × 500 g whole sea bass or red snapper, cleaned and descaled
4-5 red and green bird's-eye chiles, chopped
1 tablespoon fish sauce, for the topping
1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar, for the topping

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Put the mango, carrot, shallots, fish sauce lime juice, and superfine (caster) sugar in a large bowl and mix well. Set aside.

Butterfly the fish by cutting the fish lengthwise down the middle to the backbone, without cutting all the way through, then open out to create a butterfly fillet, leaving the head and bones intact. Pat dry with paper towels.

Heat the oil for deep-frying in a wok or deep fryer to 350°F/180°C or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds. Deep-fry the sea bass for 15 minutes, or until golden brown and crispy. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Set aside 1 tablespoon of the oil.
For the fish topping, put the fish sauce and sugar in a small bowl and mix until the sugar has dissolved.

Heat the reserved oil in a wok over medium heat, add the fish sauce and palm sugar mixture, and heat for 1 minute or until it starts sizzling. Pour the sizzling mixture over the fish and top with the mango and carrot. Serve.

steps: Cut the sea bass fillets into 2 cm cubes. Toss the cubes with the flour, then coat the reserved fish bones with the remaining flour.

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Butterfly each fish by cutting lengthwise down the middle to the backbone without cutting all the way through. Open it into a butterfly fillet, leaving the head and bones intact, and pat dry with paper towels.
Rub the fish with the salt. Place on a large plate, cover, and marinate in the refrigerator for 2-3 hours.
Rinse thoroughly, drain, wrap in cheesecloth, and sun-dry for 1-2 hours. Alternatively, heat the oven to 60°C and dry the fish for 11⁄2-2 hours.
Heat the oil in a deep, heavy pan or deep fryer to 180°C. Cut the fish into pieces and deep-fry for 10-15 minutes, until golden.
Remove with a slotted spoon, drain on paper towels, and serve with glutinous rice and tomato chili sauce.

recipes.title: Fish Cakes

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 300 g skinless spotted featherback, cod, or salmon fillets, ground (minced)
1 tablespoon thinly sliced kaffir lime leaves
750 ml vegetable oil, for deep-frying Cucumber Relish (see p. 85), to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Mix the fish and curry paste together by hand in a bowl until thoroughly combined.
Add the egg, sugar, fish sauce, cornstarch, and salt and mix well. Add the beans and kaffir lime leaves and continue mixing until the mixture is firm and sticky.
Cover and chill in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour.
Dampen your hands and shape the mixture into 20-25 round cakes, about 5 cm in diameter and 7-8 mm thick.
Heat the oil in a wok or deep fryer to 180°C. Deep-fry the fish cakes in batches for 3-4 minutes, until golden brown.
Remove with a slotted spoon, drain on paper towels, and serve with cucumber relish.

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 400 g cobia or another white fish such as tilapia, halved crosswise
2 scallions (spring onions), cut into 5 cm lengths

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Spread the flour on a plate and coat both sides of the fish in it.

Heat the deep-frying oil in a wok or deep fryer to 350°F/180°C. Deep-fry the fish for 6-8 minutes, until golden brown. Remove with a slotted spoon, drain on paper towels, and transfer to a serving plate.

Heat the remaining 3 tablespoons oil in a clean wok or skillet over medium heat. Add the garlic, shallot, and lemongrass and sauté for 2-3 minutes, until the shallot has softened and the lemongrass is lightly browned.

Add the tamarind, broth, soy sauce, and sugar. Stir for 4-5 minutes, until the sugar dissolves and the sauce thickens. Add the chile and scallions and cook for 1 minute more. Pour over the fish and serve.

recipes.title: Deep-Fried Pork and Crabmeat in Shells
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 475 ml vegetable oil, for deep-frying Red, green, and orange bell peppers, seeded and sliced, to garnish Sweet Chili Dipping Sauce (see p. 60), to serve Lettuce leaves, to serve

steps: Combine the pork, water chestnuts, crabmeat, and onions in a large bowl. Add the cilantro roots and soy sauce and mix well.

Beat the eggs with the flour in a bowl until thoroughly combined.
Heat the oil in a large wok or deep fryer to 180°C. Dip each steamed, filled shell into the egg mixture until coated, then carefully lower it into the oil.
Deep-fry for 4-6 minutes, until golden brown and crisp. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels; repeat with the remaining shells.
Arrange on lettuce leaves, garnish with the sliced peppers, and serve with sweet chili dipping sauce.

lines: 600 g sea bass fillets, cut into 2.5 cm dice
10 cm piece fresh ginger, peeled and diced

steps: For the sauce, heat a wok over medium heat. Add the sugar and fish sauce and stir for 4-5 minutes, until thick. Remove from the heat, add the lime juice and pickled plum juice, and stir until combined. Transfer to a small serving bowl.
Heat the oil for deep-frying to 180°C, or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds. Deep-fry the fish for 6-7 minutes or until golden brown. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Lay the kale leaves on a large serving plate and place a couple of fish pieces in the center of each leaf. Top with the ginger, limes, chiles, shallot, and peanuts. Serve with the sauce.

ingredientGroups.heading: For the sauce
lines: 3 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar

lines: 3 hard-boiled eggs, peeled and halved sliced cucumber

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Bring a large pan of water to a boil over high heat. Carefully place the pork side (belly), skin side down, in the pan and return to a boil. Add half the salt, then reduce the heat to medium and simmer for 30 minutes. Transfer to a wire rack, let rest for 5-10 minutes, then pierce the skin all over with a fork. Rub with the vinegar, then the remaining salt. Score the skin in a 1 cm crisscross pattern and set aside. Preheat the oven to 375°F/190°C/Gas Mark 5. Transfer the seasoned pork to a large roasting pan, skin side up, and roast for about 11⁄2 hours. Remove and set aside.

Meanwhile, make the sauce. Bring 250 ml water, the broth (stock), and cilantro (coriander) root to a boil in a pan over medium heat. Add the remaining ingredients except the cornstarch (cornflour) and boil for 5 minutes or until the mixture has slightly reduced and is thoroughly combined.
Dissolve the cornstarch in 4 tablespoons water and add to the pan, stirring well. Let the sauce boil for another 2 minutes or until thickened.

Heat the oil in a skillet or frying pan over medium heat. Sauté the pork, skin side down, for 2-3 minutes or until the skin is puffed up and crisped, then turn and saute the other side for another 1-2 minutes. Remove, drain, and let cooL.
Slice the cooled pork into bite-size pieces and place on top of the rice. Pour over the sauce and serve with the egg and cucumber.

Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.

Remove half the oil from the wok or deep fryer, reduce the heat to low, and add the pounded garlic mixture. Deep-fry for 1-2 minutes until brown. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Let cool.
Place the ribs on a serving plate, sprinkle with the crispy garlic, and serve with steamed rice and sliced cucumber.

Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Remove half the oil from the wok or deep fryer, reduce the heat to low, and add the pounded garlic mixture. Place the ribs on a serving plate, sprinkle with the crispy garlic, and serve with steamed rice and sliced cucumber.

recipes.title: Deep-Fried Bottle Gourd
recipes.subtitle: North

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 ×400 g young bottle gourd, cut into 1⁄2 × 3-inch/1 × 7 cm sticks

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the dipping sauce, soak the dried chiles in a bowl of warm water for 15 minutes or until rehydrated, then drain and chop.

Pound the chiles, garlic, and tamarind in a mortar with a pestle. Add the salt, sugar, and 1 tablespoon water, then add the cilantro (coriander) and mix together until the salt ana sugar have dissolved. Transfer to a small serving bowl and set aside Spread the tempura batter mix out on a plate and dip the gourd sticks into the batter mix until well coated.

Heat the oil for deep-frying in a wok or deep fryer to 350°F/180°C or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds. Deep-fry the coated gourd in batches for 4-5 minutes until golden brown. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Transfer the gourd slices to a serving plate, season with the salt, and serve with the dipping sauce.

recipes.title: Deep-Fried Salted Chicken
recipes.subtitle: North

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 400 g boneless chicken thighs, cut into 2.5 cm cubes
1 teaspoon granulated sugar pinch of white pepper
2 red spur chiles, diagonally sliced, to garnish

ingredientGroups.heading: For the roasted chili dip
lines: 10 dried red bird's eye chiles, seeded

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Combine the chicken, garlic, soy sauce, salt, pepper, and sugar in a bowl. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for 10-15 minutes.

For the chili dip, toast the dried chiles in a wok over medium heat for 2-3 minutes, or until fragrant and dark. Remove and set aside. Toast the garlic and shallot for 2-3 minutes, or until soft and lightly burned.

Transfer the garlic and shallot to a mortar. Add the toasted chiles, galangal, and shrimp paste and pound until smooth. Add the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, and 2 tablespoons water and stir well. Transfer to a serving bowl.

Heat the oil for deep-frying to 350°F/180°C. Deep-fry the chicken for 8-10 minutes, or until golden and crisp. Drain on paper towels, garnish with the sliced red chiles, and serve with the roasted chili dip.

recipes.searchText: Deep-Fried Salted Chicken North 400 g boneless chicken thighs, cut into 2.5 cm cubes 5 cloves garlic, crushed 1 tablespoon soy sauce 11⁄2 teaspoons salt 1 teaspoon granulated sugar pinch of white pepper 475 ml vegetable oil, for deep-frying 2 red spur chiles, diagonally sliced, to garnish 10 dried red bird's eye chiles, seeded 3 cloves garlic, halved 1 shallot, quartered 1 slice galangal, chopped 1 teaspoon shrimp paste 11⁄2 tablespoons fish sauce 1 tablespoon lime juice 11⁄2 teaspoons granulated sugar Combine the chicken, garlic, soy sauce, salt, pepper, and sugar in a bowl. Add the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, and 2 tablespoons water and stir well. Transfer to a serving bowl. Heat the oil for deep-frying to 350°F/180°C. Deep-fry the chicken for 8-10 minutes, or until golden and crisp. Drain on paper towels, garnish with the sliced red chiles, and serve with the roasted chili dip.

recipes.title: Raw Soft-Shell Crab in Fish Sauce
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 10-15 red and green bird's eye chiles, chopped

ingredientGroups.heading: To serve
lines: 1 bitter gourd, peeled and thinly sliced
3 cloves garlic, peeled and left whole

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Rinse the crabs under cold running water.

Using a pair of sharp scissors, cut off the front part of the crab behind the eyes, then open the top shell and remove and discard the gills. Turn the crab over and remove the apron. Repeat with the remaining crabs.

Place the crabs on a plate with 3 tablespoons fish sauce. Cover with plastic wrap (clingfilm) and let marinate in the refrigerator for 2 hours. Pound the garlic and the chiles together in a mortar with a pestle. Add the lime juice, sugar, and the remaining fish sauce and stir until thoroughly combined.
Place the marinated crabs on a serving plate and drizzle with the sauce, Arrange the bitter gourd around the crabs and sprinkle with the mint and the whole garlic cloves. Serve.

recipes.searchText: Raw Soft-Shell Crab in Fish Sauce Central 3 live soft-shell crabs 75 ml fish sauce 15 cloves garlic, chopped 10-15 red and green bird's eye chiles, chopped 1 tablespoon lime juice 1 tablespoon granulated sugar 1 bitter gourd, peeled and thinly sliced 2-3 mint sprigs 3 cloves garlic, peeled and left whole Rinse the crabs under cold running water. Using a pair of sharp scissors, cut off the front part of the crab behind the eyes, then open the top shell and remove and discard the gills. Turn the crab over and remove the apron. recipes.title: Spicy Water Spinach and Shrimp Salad
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 4 uncooked jumbo shrimp (king prawns), peeled and deveined, with tails still intact
3 red finger chiles, sliced into fine strips

ingredientGroups.heading: For the batter
lines: 120 g wheat flour pinch of salt pinch of ground black pepper

ingredientGroups.heading: For the sauce
lines: 1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: To make the batter, put the flour, salt, and black pepper into a bowl and stir to combine. Add 175 ml water and stir until a batter forms.
Coat the water spinach in the batter.

Heat the oil for deep-frying in a wok or deep fryer to 350°F/180°C or until a cube of bread browns in 30 seconds. Gradually add the coated water spinach to the hot oil, and deep- fry for 4-5 minutes or until cooked. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Deep-fry the shrimp (prawns) for 2-3 minutes or until cooked. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Set aside. For the sauce, bring the coconut milk and fish sauce to a boil in a separate wok over medium heat. Add the sugar, chili jam, and lime juice stir, and return to a boil. Remove from the heat.
To serve, place the deep-fried water spinach and shrimp on a serving plate and pour over the sauce. Sprinkle with the chiles and fried shallots and serve.

recipes.searchText: Spicy Water Spinach and Shrimp Salad Central 150 g water spinach, sliced 250 ml vegetable oil, for deep-frying 4 uncooked jumbo shrimp (king prawns), peeled and deveined, with tails still intact 3 red finger chiles, sliced into fine strips 3 tablespoons Fried Shallots (see p. 64) 120 g wheat flour pinch of salt pinch of ground black pepper 80 ml coconut milk 2 tablespoons fish sauce 1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar 1 tablespoon Chili Jam (see p. 35) 2 tablespoons lime juice To make the batter, put the flour, salt, and black pepper into a bowl and stir to combine. To serve, place the deep-fried water spinach and shrimp on a serving plate and pour over the sauce. Sprinkle with the chiles and fried shallots and serve.

recipes.title: Pork Floss Wrapped in Kale Leaves
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 5 cm piece fresh ginger, peeled and cut into 1 cm dice
10-15 red and green bird's-eye chiles, finely chopped

ingredientGroups.heading: For the sweet-and-sour dressing
lines: 21⁄2 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the dressing, mix the sugar, fish sauce, lime juice, and pickled plum juice, if using, in a pan over medium heat. Stir for about 2 minutes, or until the sugar has dissolved and starts to caramelize. Let cool.
Mix the ginger, chiles, shallots, lemongrass, roasted peanuts, limes, pork floss, and dressing together in a large bowl.
To serve, place the kale leaves on a serving plate and put a teaspoon of the pork mixture into the center of each leaf.

recipes.searchText: Pork Floss Wrapped in Kale Leaves Central 5 cm piece fresh ginger, peeled and cut into 1 cm dice 10-15 red and green bird's-eye chiles, finely chopped 4 shallots, chopped into 8 mm pieces 4 lemongrass stalks, finely sliced 40 g roasted peanuts 2 limes, cut into 1 cm dice 100 g pork floss 20 young Chinese kale leaves 21⁄2 tablespoons jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar 1 tablespoon fish sauce 1 tablespoon lime juice 11⁄2 teaspoons pickled plum juice (optional) For the dressing, mix the sugar, fish sauce, lime juice, and pickled plum juice, if using, in a pan over medium heat. Mix the ginger, chiles, shallots, lemongrass, roasted peanuts, limes, pork floss, and dressing together in a large bowl. To serve, place the kale leaves on a serving plate and put a teaspoon of the pork mixture into the center of each leaf.

recipes.title: Spicy Raw Shrimp in Fish Sauce
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 15 raw shrimp, peeled and deveined with tails intact
5 red and green bird's-eye chiles, to garnish
100 g sliced bitter gourd, to garnish
5 garlic cloves, thinly sliced lengthwise, to garnish

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Arrange the uncooked shrimp (prawns) on a serving plate.

Mix the fish sauce with 11⁄2 tablespoons water in a bowl, then pour over the shrimp. Cover the plate with plastic wrap (clingfilm) and chill in the refrigerator for 30-50 minutes or until the shrimp have absorbed the sauce.
To serve, pour the seafood sauce over the shrimp and garnish with the chiles, bitter gourd, garlic, and mint leaves.

recipes.searchText: Spicy Raw Shrimp in Fish Sauce Central 15 raw shrimp, peeled and deveined with tails intact 11⁄2 teaspoons fish sauce 60 ml Seafood Dipping Sauce (see p. 58) 5 red and green bird's-eye chiles, to garnish 100 g sliced bitter gourd, to garnish 5 garlic cloves, thinly sliced lengthwise, to garnish 15 mint leaves, to garnish Arrange the uncooked shrimp (prawns) on a serving plate. Mix the fish sauce with 11⁄2 tablespoons water in a bowl, then pour over the shrimp. Cover the plate with plastic wrap (clingfilm) and chill in the refrigerator for 30-50 minutes or until the shrimp have absorbed the sauce. recipes.title: Stir-Fried Angled Gourd with Egg
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1-2 x 400 g angled gourds, peeled and sliced
1 teaspoon fish sauce à teaspoon granulated sugar

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over high heat, add the garlic, and stir-fry for 30 seconds or until fragrant. Add the gourds and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes. Add the eggs and stir-fry for another minute or until the eggs are cooked. Add the oyster sauce, soy sauce, fish sauce, and sugar and mix well. Serve.

recipes.searchText: Stir-Fried Angled Gourd with Egg Central 2 tablespoons vegetable oil 3 cloves garlic, crushed 1-2 x 400 g angled gourds, peeled and sliced 2 eggs 1 tablespoon oyster sauce 1 teaspoon soy sauce 1 teaspoon fish sauce à teaspoon granulated sugar Heat the oil in a wok over high heat, add the garlic, and stir-fry for 30 seconds or until fragrant. Add the gourds and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes. Add the eggs and stir-fry for another minute or until the eggs are cooked. Add the oyster sauce, soy sauce, fish sauce, and sugar and mix well. Serve.

recipes.title: Stir-Fried Tofu with Bean Sprouts
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 100 g extra firm tofu, cut into 2 cm cubes

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the tofu, and stir-fry for 4-5 minutes or until golden. Remove with a slotted spoon and set aside. Reserve 2 tablespoons of the oil, then drain the rest from the wok. Increase the heat to medium-high and heat the reserved oil. Add the garlic and bean sprouts and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes. Add the chiles, scallions (spring onions), oyster sauce, soy sauce, and tofu and stir-fry for another 1 minute. Serve.

recipes.searchText: Stir-Fried Tofu with Bean Sprouts Central 250 ml vegetable oil 100 g extra firm tofu, cut into 2 cm cubes 8 cloves garlic, finely chopped 300 g bean sprouts 3 red spur chiles, diagonally sliced 2 scallions (spring onions), sliced into 1-inch 3 cm.length: 2 tablespoons oyster sauce 1 teaspoon soy sauce Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the tofu, and stir-fry for 4-5 minutes or until golden. recipes.title: Spicy Stir-Fried Basa Fish
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 1 ×400 g whole basa fish or river cobbler, cleaned
120 g finely sliced heart of palm
7 fresh young green peppercorns, on their stalks

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Cut through the basa fish belly and remove the innards, then cut the fish into slices and rinse under cold running water. Drain and set aside.
Roughly pound all the chiles, sliced fingerroot, and garlic together in a mortar with a pestle.

Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the chile mixture and stir-fry for 1 minute or until fragrant. Add the sliced fish and stir-fry for 8 minutes. Add the remaining ingredients and stir-fry for 2 minutes. Serve.

recipes.searchText: Spicy Stir-Fried Basa Fish Central 1 ×400 g whole basa fish or river cobbler, cleaned 3 tablespoons vegetable oil 4-6 kaffir lime leaves, ripped 3 sweet basil sprigs, leaves only 120 g finely sliced heart of palm 3 round eggplants (aubergines), quartered 7 fresh young green peppercorns, on their stalks 1 teaspoon granulated sugar 2 tablespoons soy sauce 5 red and green bird's-eye chiles 7 orange finger chiles, pounded 3-4 red finger chiles, sliced 50 g peeled and sliced fingerroots 5 cloves garlic Cut through the basa fish belly and remove the innards, then cut the fish into slices and rinse under cold running water. recipes.title: Stir-Fried Fish with Vegetables
recipes.subtitle: North

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 300 g white fish fillet, cut into K 1 cm slices
5 fresh young green peppercorns (on their stalks)
2 yard-long beans, cut into 5 cm long lengths

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Pound the garlic, shallot, and bird's eye chile thoroughly in a mortar with a pestle, then set aside.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the fish, and cook for 2-3 minutes until cooked. Transfer the fish to a plate.

Add the pounded mixture to the wok and stir-fry for 1 minute or until fragrant. Add the fish, fingerroot, peppercorns, eggplant (aubergine), baby corn, yard-long beans, and kaffir lime leaves and stir-fry for 1 minute Season with the fish sauce, oyster sauce, and sugar and mix well. Add the basil and red spur chiles, then serve.

recipes.title: Spicy Stir-Fried Fish with Mixed Vegetables

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 500 g clown featherback fish or cod fillet, cut into bite-size pieces
3 red and green finger chiles, chopped
1 tablespoon jaggery, palm sugar, or soft light brown sugar
4 fresh young green peppercorns (on their stalks). to garnish

ingredientGroups.heading: For the chili paste
lines: 1 Kaffir lime leaf, torn zest of 1 kaffir lime

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: For the chili paste, soak the dried chiles in a bowl of warm water for 15 minutes or until rehydrated, then drain and chop. Transfer to a mortar with the remaining chili paste ingredients and pound with a pestle until smooth. Set aside.

Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the chili paste, and stir-fry for 1 minute or until fragrant. Add the fish, basil, chiles, fingerroot, eggplant (aubergine), yard-long beans, fish sauce, and sugar and stir-fry for 3 minutes or until cooked. Garnish with the green peppercorns and serve.

recipes.title: Stir-Fried Spanish Mackerel with Celery
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 300 g Spanish mackerel fillet, sliced into 3-4 cm pieces
150 g Chinese celery, chopped into 5 cm lengths Steamed Jasmine Rice (see p. 378), to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Spread the flour on a plate, coat the fish pieces in it, and set aside.
Heat the oil in a wok or deep fryer to 180°C. Deep-fry the mackerel for 5-7 minutes, until golden brown. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Drain all but 2 tablespoons oil from the wok and heat over medium heat. Add the garlic and stir-fry for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Reduce the heat to low. Add the oyster sauce, soy sauce, sugar, salted soybeans, and broth and stir.
Add the fried fish, chiles, and celery and stir-fry for 20 seconds, until thoroughly combined. Serve with rice.

Add the oyster sauce, soy sauce, sugar, salted soybeans, and broth and stir. Add the fried fish, chiles, and celery and stir-fry for 20 seconds, until thoroughly combined. Serve with rice.

recipes.title: Stir-Fried Sea Bass with Cardamom Shoots

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 300 g sea bass fillet, cut into 1 cm pieces
50 g sweet basil leaves, plus extra to serve

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Pound the chiles and garlic together in a mortar with a pestle until smooth.

Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the paste, and stir-fry for 1 minute or until fragrant. Add the sea bass and fish sauce and cook for 3-5 minutes. Add the cardamom shoots and basil and cook for another 2 minutes. Serve with extra cardamom shoots, sweet basil, and garlic cloves.

recipes.searchText: Stir-Fried Sea Bass with Cardamom Shoots Central 3-5 orange finger chiles, chopped 5-10 cloves garlic, chopped 3 tablespoons vegetable oil 300 g sea bass fillet, cut into 1 cm pieces 11⁄2 tablespoons fish sauce 120 g chopped Siamese cardamom shoots 50 g sweet basil leaves, plus extra to serve Pound the chiles and garlic together in a mortar with a pestle until smooth. Add the cardamom shoots and basil and cook for another 2 minutes. Serve with extra cardamom shoots, sweet basil, and garlic cloves.

recipes.title: Stir-Fried Snakehead Fish with Salted Soybeans
recipes.subtitle: Central

ingredientGroups.heading: Ingredients
lines: 300 g snakehead, catfish, or tilapia fish fillet, cut into bite-size pieces
10 cm piece fresh ginger, peeled and finely julienned
5 green finger chiles, cut into strips
150 g chopped Chinese celery, cut into 5 cm lengths

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Soak the dried mushrooms in a bowl of boiling water for 10 minutes or until softened. Drain and set aside.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok over medium heat. Add the garlic and stir-fry for 1 minute or until fragrant.

Add the fish and stir-fry gently for 3 minutes or until cooked. Add the salted soybeans, sesame oil, oyster sauce, soy sauce, sugar, pepper, and 2 tablespoons water. Stir-fry for 3 minutes, until thoroughly combined.
Add the ginger and cloud ear mushrooms and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes, until the mushrooms are cooked. Add the green chiles and Chinese celery and stir 2-3 times, until well mixed. Serve.

recipes.title: Stir-Fried Kale with Salted Fish

100 g sun-dried salted fish (Spanish mackerel). rinsed, dried, and cut into bite-size pieces

methodGroups.heading: Method
steps: Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat and add the Fried Garlic, chiles, and fish. Then add the kale and stir-fry for about 4 minutes until cooked. Add the oyster sauce and sugar and serve.

recipes.searchText: Stir-Fried Kale with Salted Fish Central 2 tablespoons vegetable oil 2 tablespoons Fried Garlic (see p. 64) 2 red bird's eye chiles, chopped and pounded 100 g sun-dried salted fish (Spanish mackerel). rinsed, dried, and cut into bite-size pieces 5-7 Chinese kale stems, chopped 1 teaspoon oyster sauce 1⁄2 teaspoon superfine (caster) sugar Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat and add the Fried Garlic, chiles, and fish.
